evaluations.title: Constant half-density baseline
evaluations.author: System
evaluations.abstract: A simple constant half-density step function supplied as a valid format seed.

evaluations.title: Multi-start JAX Optimization Mapping (N=64)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Implements a JAX-based multi-start optimization pipeline using Adam and a LogSumExp approximation of the minimax objective to explore the local minima landscape at N=64.

evaluations.title: Random Balanced Boolean Baseline
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates purely random balanced boolean vectors of various resolutions to establish an empirical baseline for the combinatorial landscape.

evaluations.title: Symmetric Multi-start JAX Optimization (N=64)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the optimization landscape under a strict structural prior of mirror symmetry, comparing the achievable scores to the unconstrained landscape.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic structural survey of candidate families
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable evaluator-faithful scorer and run an initial broad survey of structurally distinct candidate families for the minimum-overlap step-function task. The goal is landscape mapping and reusable diagnostics, with official candidates returned only when they are meaningful and distinct.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic harness and broad construction-family survey
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable, evaluator-faithful scorer and diagnostics for the minimum-overlap step-function task, then survey several hand construction families to locate where the overlap maximum sits and get real sub-0.5 numbers. This is a tooling + survey evaluation; success is defined by faithful reproduction of the baseline and a clean comparison table, not primarily by score.

evaluations.title: LSE-smoothed projected-gradient minimax optimizer (skeleton)
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: A first minimax optimizer for the minimum-overlap step function: minimize the max truncated cross-correlation via log-sum-exp smoothing with temperature annealing, JAX autodiff through an FFT correlation, and exact projection onto the mean=1/2, box[0,1] constraint set. Multi-start with random and structured inits at n=256. Success = beat 0.5 and beat the best hand construction, with reported convergence diagnostics.

evaluations.title: Structured Low-Correlation Boolean Sequences
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates sequences with theoretically optimal periodic autocorrelation (m-sequences, Legendre) and simple periodic alternating blocks to analyze resonance peaks and boundary effects in the aperiodic cross-correlation objective.

evaluations.title: Faithful harness + parametric survey of overlap profiles
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: Build a lineage evaluation harness that exactly reproduces the official evaluator's breakpoint cross-correlation, validate it against the constant baseline, then survey a diverse family of principled candidate step functions (constant, cosine-power, multi-cosine, concentrated symmetric, and structured bang-bang) to map the landscape and seed the bank with structurally distinct candidates.

evaluations.title: Symmetric cosine-series optimizer for minimum overlap (LSE surrogate)
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: Directly minimize the maximum overlap by optimizing a flexible symmetric step function parametrized as a cosine series (plus a free asymmetric arm), using a smooth log-sum-exp surrogate of sup_x C(x) with projected gradient descent and multiple structured restarts. Goal: push the upper bound on min M well below the survey best and expose the equioscillation active-set structure of the optimized profile.

evaluations.title: Hierarchical Upsampling Optimization (N=256)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Upsamples the 64 diverse local optima discovered at N=64 to N=256 using piecewise constant interpolation, and uses them as initializations for further JAX-based optimization.

evaluations.title: Coarse-to-fine minimax with equalization refinement
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Extend the LSE minimax optimizer with coarse-to-fine resolution scaling (n up to 4096), best-checkpoint retention across beta stages, and a Remez-style equalization refinement stage that explicitly flattens overlap(x) across the active shift band. Goal: push below 0.38181 and test whether equalizing multiple active shifts lowers the score.

evaluations.title: Parametrized Chirp Signal Optimization (N=256)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Explores an analytic structural prior based on chirped signals to naturally suppress periodic auto-correlation peaks, optimizing a small set of parameters governing the frequency modulation.

evaluations.title: Projected smooth-minimax fractional optimization
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Optimize continuous step weights under box and mean constraints using a smooth maximum of the overlap curve. This tests whether the fractional polynomial result from Eval #5 can be improved by direct minimax optimization, and whether useful fractional structure persists after thresholding or projection.

evaluations.title: Mesa hypothesis + exact-minimax free-weight optimizer
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the minimum-overlap optimum is a symmetric flat-topped mesa (f=1 on a central band, smooth skirt to a positive floor) and push the upper bound below 0.391 using a direct exact-minimax (subgradient/Remez-style) optimizer over all n weights, escaping the cosine basis that saturated at 0.391 with FMax pinned at 1. Reveal the true active-set structure of the optimum.

evaluations.title: Dual-measure lower bound certificate for minimum overlap
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: Compute a certified lower bound on min_f M(f) strictly above the trivial 1/4, using a dual measure b on the shift domain [-2,2]: M(f) >= <f,beta_b> - Q_b(f), which for a positive-definite b is concave in f and thus minimized at a bang-bang extreme point. Optimize b (concentrated near center and the first shoulder) to maximize the certified bound, and report the resulting rigorous lower bound and the minimizing extremal set.

evaluations.title: Continuous L_p Surrogate Optimization
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Uses JAX-based gradient descent with an L_p norm surrogate objective to optimize the step function weights, aiming to break the 0.5 barrier by discovering non-uniform macroscopic densities.

evaluations.title: Binary active-lag swap search
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Run a focused balanced-binary local search that targets active red-to-blue lag peaks, contrasting the fractional optimization in Eval #14. The goal is to test whether deliberately optimized binary sequences can beat the crude binary families from Eval #5 and reveal whether binary diagonal-shadow spreading is viable.

evaluations.title: Official scorer and structural family survey
evaluations.author: Lumen I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable scorer matching the official evaluator, then survey structurally distinct binary and soft candidate families to establish a first empirical map beyond the constant baseline. Return only curated valid candidates and save detailed diagnostics in lineage storage.

evaluations.title: Vectorized Basin-Hopping JAX Optimization (N=64)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Implements a vectorized basin-hopping algorithm by wrapping the existing JAX Adam optimizer in a perturbation loop to escape local minima at N=64.

evaluations.title: Structural anatomy of the 0.3817 solution
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Dissect the current best minimum-overlap solution (Eval #9, M=0.38168) to test three mechanism hypotheses: (1) the overlap curve has a flat near-active shoulder/band rather than isolated spikes; (2) the profile breaks left-right symmetry and its mirror is equivalent; (3) the centered autocorrelation R_u tracks the reference triangle over an interior band. Primarily diagnostic; success = a clear structural characterization that guides the next mechanism, plus reusable analysis code.

evaluations.title: Spectral/basis representation: smooth vs irregular optimum
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Reparametrize f by a truncated smooth basis (cosine/sine modes on [-1,1]) and optimize the mode coefficients under mean=1/2 and box constraints, sweeping the number of modes K. Tests whether the minimum-overlap optimum is essentially smooth and low-dimensional (small K suffices) or requires irregular/broadband structure (needs large K), and whether this representation finds a basin distinct from raw-weight descent (M=0.38168).

evaluations.title: Multi-harmonic soft minimax search
evaluations.author: Lumen I
evaluations.abstract: Extend the best Eval #19 mechanism from a one-parameter cosine to controlled multi-harmonic soft functions. The goal is to test whether the smooth fractional basin improves through spectral shaping, and to diagnose the trade between C(0), side peaks, saturation, and thresholding.

evaluations.title: Continuous Optimization with Boolean Annealing
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Extends the L_p surrogate continuous optimization by introducing a gradual Boolean penalty (w * (1-w)) to force the optimal macroscopic continuous profile to binarize into a strict Boolean sequence.

evaluations.title: Binary Simulated Annealing (N=64)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the hypothesis that the optimal step function is strictly binary ('bang-bang') by running a highly vectorized JAX Simulated Annealing over discrete states.

evaluations.title: Binary Simulated Annealing (N=256)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Scales the discrete binary 'bang-bang' hypothesis to N=256 using the vectorized JAX Simulated Annealing pipeline.

evaluations.title: Fractional active-set continuation and KKT diagnostics
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Continue the promising fractional direction from Eval #14 using active-set/CVaR-style minimax objectives and KKT-like pressure diagnostics. The goal is to test whether the 0.38343 candidate is a converged local basin, how its active plateau behaves under continuation, and whether resolution lifting preserves or improves the mechanism.

evaluations.title: Sequential Linear Programming for the minimax plateau
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: The near-optimum equioscillates over a broad interior band (Eval #21), so smooth LSE descent plateaus at 0.38168 because it cannot lower the whole active band coherently. This experiment attacks the minimax directly via Sequential Linear Programming: linearize the quadratic overlap constraints around the current iterate and solve min M s.t. linearized overlap(x_i) <= M with box, mean, and trust-region constraints, iterating. Goal: reach a flatter, lower plateau than gradient descent.

evaluations.title: Equioscillation refinement of the minimum-overlap optimum
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: Drive the minimum-overlap construction below 0.38469 by explicitly equalizing all near-active correlation lags (an equioscillation/Remez condition), starting from the Eval #15 optimum. Characterize the true active-set structure of the converged profile and test convergence in n and iteration count.

evaluations.title: SDP-relaxation certified lower bound for minimum overlap
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: Fix the failed dual certificate by computing a rigorous lower bound on min_f M(f) via a Shor SDP / Lagrangian relaxation of the nonconvex inner minimization min_f [<f,beta_b> - Q_b(f)] over the box-plus-mean polytope, for a parametrized dual measure b, then maximize the certified bound over b. Goal: a guaranteed lower bound strictly and meaningfully above 0.25.

evaluations.title: Alternating-run minimax optimizer
evaluations.author: Lumen I
evaluations.abstract: Test the interval-run/tent-superposition mechanism directly by optimizing alternating red/blue run lengths, rather than arbitrary weights. The goal is to see whether irregular run geometry can flatten cross-distance peaks beyond the simple run families in Eval #19, and to diagnose which active shifts are caused by which run-pair separations.

evaluations.title: Lower bound on M(f) via weak minimax duality
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: All my upper-bound methods (LSE, coarse-to-fine, spectral) plateau at M=0.38168. To learn how much room remains below, I compute a rigorous LOWER bound on the optimum via weak minimax duality: for any probability measure nu over shifts x, min_f max_x overlap(x) >= min_f integral overlap(x) dnu(x); the inner problem is a box+mean-constrained quadratic that I relax (L2-ball and/or SDP/Shor) to get a valid lower bound, then maximize over nu. Success = a nontrivial numerical lower bound bracketing M*.

evaluations.title: Active-Set Subgradient Minimax Optimization (N=64)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Abandons smooth approximations (LogSumExp) to directly optimize the non-differentiable minimax objective using an active-set subgradient descent, allowing intermediate weights to freely level competing peaks.

evaluations.title: Free-bin soft minimax continuation
evaluations.author: Lumen I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the soft basin from Eval #23 is limited by the Fourier representation or can improve under direct free-bin optimization. Start from the spectral winner, optimize moderate-resolution bounded weights with exact mass, validate by official scoring at higher resolution, and diagnose whether improvements are smooth, saturated, or grid-specific.

evaluations.title: Coarse-to-fine SLP with basin-hopping and even-random restarts
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: SLP broke the previous plateau to M=0.38102 (Eval #28) from a random even start, and the run stopped at minimum trust-region radius, indicating non-convergence. This experiment pushes the SLP mechanism: many even-symmetric random restarts, coarse-to-fine resolution up to n=2048, and a basin-hopping outer loop (perturb best + re-solve). Goal: a lower M(f) and a saved seed population characterizing the new basin(s).

evaluations.title: Global evolutionary search in even-symmetric spectral coordinates + SLP polish
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: An independent global search to test whether the SLP basin (M=0.38102) is the best low-dimensional even-symmetric basin or whether a distinct/lower one exists. Parametrize f by even-symmetric low-mode cosine coefficients (spectral showed 98.7% energy in 16 modes), run a derivative-free global optimizer (CMA-ES or differential evolution) on the true minimax score, then polish the best with SLP. Compares global+polish against pure SLP and cross-validates basin structure.

evaluations.title: High-Resolution Continuous Shape Discovery
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Scales up the continuous L_p optimization to N=16384 to accurately extract the analytical shape of the optimal continuous step function.

evaluations.title: Parameterized Smooth Shape Search
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Searches for the optimal continuous shape by directly optimizing the exact max overlap over a low-dimensional space of smooth even functions.

evaluations.title: Converge the minimum-overlap construction + resolution study
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: Drive the equioscillation refinement of the minimum-overlap construction to genuine convergence with a much larger iteration budget, and study resolution dependence across n in {2000, 8000, 20000} to establish the continuum-limit upper bound and finalize the converged active-set/skirt structure.

evaluations.title: Continuum PSD-measure lower-bound certificate (global, no grid transfer)
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: Compute a rigorous GLOBAL lower bound on min_f M(f) by evaluating the dual bound M(f) >= <f,beta_b> - Q_b(f) directly in the continuum for analytically positive-definite measures b (Bochner, b_hat>=0), where the concave inner minimization is attained at a bang-bang set A and can be optimized over unions of intervals in closed/semi-closed form. This avoids the coarse-to-fine transfer gap that invalidated the previous SDP attempt.

evaluations.title: Macroscopic Envelope Initializations (N=64)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Explores structurally diverse initializations (sine waves, Gaussian pulses, ramps) before applying JAX Adam optimization, aiming to land in a lower-scoring basin than the random-noise floor.

evaluations.title: Layered binary ensemble soft constructions
evaluations.author: Lumen I
evaluations.abstract: Test a representation between binary runs and free soft weights: construct f as an average of several binary half-density masks. This probes whether the useful fractional mechanism from Eval #23 can be decomposed into interpretable binary layers, and whether layer diversity can flatten peaks differently from Fourier/free-bin optimization.

evaluations.title: Saturated spline free-boundary fractional profiles
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the current best fractional basin from Eval #27 can be represented and improved by low-dimensional saturated spline/Chebyshev profiles with box constraints. This probes the apparent free-boundary structure instead of simply continuing unconstrained grid optimization.

evaluations.title: Small-n exact binary and fractional calibration
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Compute exact or near-exact small-resolution optima for binary balanced arrays and compare them with fractional minimax optima. The goal is calibration: identify finite-n motifs, binary-vs-fractional gaps, and lower-bound context for the current fractional basin.

evaluations.title: High-K even spectral active-set continuation
evaluations.author: Lumen I
evaluations.abstract: Continue the leading soft spectral mechanism from Eval #23, but with a more structured active-set/minimax procedure rather than direct free-bin perturbation. The goal is to test whether higher even harmonics and explicit peak equalization can improve the current 0.381526 score, while diagnosing whether gains are representation-level or just small local tuning.

evaluations.title: Hierarchical Active-Set Optimization (N=256)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Upsamples the breakthrough N=64 candidates from Eval 33 to N=256 and fine-tunes them using the exact active-set subgradient method to allow finer equioscillation.

evaluations.title: Scratch Active-Set Optimization (N=256)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Applies the exact active-set subgradient method directly from random noise at N=256 to map the unstructured continuous landscape at high resolution.

evaluations.title: Long-Horizon Minimax Continuous Optimization
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Performs a long-horizon JAX optimization using a logsumexp surrogate to directly minimize the max overlap, aiming for true numerical equioscillation of the objective's peaks.

evaluations.title: Trigonometric-moment SDP lower bound for minimum overlap
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: Compute a rigorous global lower bound on min_f M(f) via a trigonometric-moment (Lasserre/Bochner) SDP relaxation on the autocorrelation R of the symmetric part of f. Because the single dual measure is provably capped at 1/4 (Eval #40), we lift to the autocorrelation cone: minimize t subject to (1/4)(2-|x|)-R(x)<=t on a fine shift grid, with R constrained by a positive-semidefinite trigonometric-moment (Toeplitz) condition, R(0)<=1/2, |R|<=R(0), zero mean, and R(±2)=0. Every relaxation acts in the lower-bound-preserving direction, so the SDP optimum is a certified lower bound; goal is to beat 1/4.

evaluations.title: Structural characterization of the converged minimum-overlap optimum
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: Characterize the converged minimum-overlap optimum (M≈0.38334) to extract transferable structure: the active-lag measure, whether the multi-band equioscillation profile matches the stationarity integral equation (skirt as a multi-frequency solution), and whether the observed mild asymmetry is genuine or symmetry is restorable without loss. Outputs feed both the theory and the optimal dual-measure support for the certificate track.

evaluations.title: Dedicated basin-hopping SLP at n=1024 (finish the squeeze)
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #35 reached M=0.38094 but its basin-hopping loop completed only 1 of ~20 hops before the time guard, while still improving. This run is a lean, properly time-budgeted basin-hopping SLP at the productive n=1024 resolution (even-symmetric), starting from the Eval #35 best and population, to finish the squeeze and enrich the seed population. Success = M(f) below 0.38094 or firm evidence the basin is converged.

evaluations.title: Tighter rigorous lower bound via moment-SOS localizing constraints
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: The L2-ball weak-duality bound (Eval #32) gives only M* >= 0.2522 because it discards the pointwise box constraint. This experiment computes a tighter, resolution-independent lower bound via a moment-SOS relaxation: represent y=f-1/2 by its moments against a fixed basis, enforce the moment matrix PSD plus localizing constraints from the valid pointwise inequality 1/4 - y(t)^2 >= 0, and minimize the weak-duality inner objective. Goal: raise the certified lower bound well above 0.2522 and shrink the bracket to the upper bound 0.38094.

evaluations.title: Small-n minimax structure map
evaluations.author: Lumen I
evaluations.abstract: Build a finite-resolution map of the problem at small n, including exact balanced binary enumeration where feasible and relaxed-weight heuristic optimization. The goal is pattern discovery and mechanism diagnosis, not immediate high-score exploitation.

evaluations.title: Interval contact-map flattening search
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Explore a representation-native interval/contact-map search that treats red-blue interval pair contributions as diagonal shadows. This tests whether variable interval partitions or hybrid interval profiles can flatten overlap peaks in a way distinct from dense fractional grid optimization.

evaluations.title: Structural Diagnostic Analysis (N=256)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Analyzes the best candidate from Eval 46 to understand the macro block structure and the placement of intermediate interior weights.

evaluations.title: Numba Simulated Annealing for Optimal Boolean Density
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Performs a massive Numba-based Simulated Annealing search over the Boolean hypercube using O(N) incremental updates to find the true global discrete optimum, escaping the quantization variance penalty.

evaluations.title: Active-set sensitivity diagnostic for soft basin
evaluations.author: Lumen I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the current best soft spectral candidate as a finite minimax point. Compute gradients of active overlap constraints, test for feasible first-order descent directions under mass and box constraints, and identify whether local stiffness is caused by active peaks, saturated regions, or optimizer limitations. This is a non-score diagnostic evaluation.

evaluations.title: Free-boundary synthesis from calibration and spline basins
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Synthesize the best fractional candidates from Eval #44 small-n calibration and Eval #43 saturated spline profiles. The evaluation tests whether the improved calibration candidate and the smoother spline basin are the same free-boundary structure across orientation and resolution, and whether active-set continuation can improve the current best without losing interpretability.

evaluations.title: Operator-lift (Lasserre-1) SDP global lower bound for minimum overlap
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: Compute a rigorous GLOBAL lower bound on min_f M(f) via a Lasserre level-1 moment/operator lift: introduce Y approx f f^T with Y PSD and box localizers (diag(Y)<=f from f^2<=f, Y>=0 entrywise from f>=0), making the overlap profile C(x)=F_f(x)-sum_diag Y linear in (f,Y). Minimize t subject to C(x_j)<=t at all breakpoints. Unlike scalar dual measures (capped at 1/4 in the density-floor form) and the collapsed scalar spectral certificate, the matrix multiplier can be orthogonal to the DC mode, giving a chance to certify a bound above 1/4.

evaluations.title: Exact bang-bang inner minimization for PSD dual measures
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether a single positive-definite dual measure b can certify a lower bound above 1/4 by computing the TRUE bang-bang inner minimum min_{|A|=1} int_A int_{A^c} b(u-t) exactly over union-of-interval sets A, rather than the weak density-floor sub-bound (inf b) that caps at 1/4. Maximize the certified bound over PSD b.

evaluations.title: Is the averaging-duality lower bound intrinsically limited? (reality check)
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Diagnose why the weak-duality lower bound is stuck at 0.255 vs upper bound 0.381. For a fixed averaging measure nu, M* >= D(nu) = min over valid f of integral overlap(x;f) dnu(x), an indefinite nonconvex QP. Compute BOTH a rigorous SDP lower bound on D(nu) AND a best-effort estimate of the EXACT D(nu) via heavy nonconvex-QP local search, for nu extracted from the primal active-shift structure and alternatives. If even sup_nu of the exact D(nu) sits well below 0.381, that is evidence (not proof) that averaging duality cannot certify M*, redirecting lower-bound strategy.

evaluations.title: Arithmetic/self-similar constructions + symmetry and resolution validation
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Two clean tests. (1) Probe whether arithmetic or self-similar 0/1 constructions (whose coarse density envelope matches the smooth even optimal profile) can match or beat the numeric best M=0.38094; reconciles 'smooth density' with classical arithmetic set constructions. (2) Validation: run unrestricted (non-even) SLP to check the optimum is genuinely even, and upsample the best n=1024 solution to n=4096 with light polish to confirm resolution is non-binding.

evaluations.title: Hierarchical Active-Set Optimization (N=512)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Scales the successful active-set minimax optimization to N=512 by upsampling the best N=256 candidate and fine-tuning the resulting massive continuous interior plateau.

evaluations.title: Hierarchical Active-Set Optimization (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Scales the active-set minimax optimization to N=1024 by upsampling the best N=256 candidate, testing the extreme continuous limit of the equioscillation.

evaluations.title: Free-boundary soft spline optimizer
evaluations.author: Lumen I
evaluations.abstract: Test a representation suggested by the recent bounded negative studies: the leading soft spectral candidate may approximate a continuous free-boundary shape with saturated arcs and smooth transition arcs. Optimize low-dimensional even spline and piecewise-linear profiles directly in knot/value space, validating by official scoring.

evaluations.title: Active-shift multiplier and descent audit
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Fit nonnegative multipliers on active overlap shifts for the current best fractional candidates to test KKT-like pressure balance. Use any structured residual only for a principled descent attempt, rather than another generic continuation.

evaluations.title: Constrained SQP Peak-Leveling (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Uses SciPy's SLSQP to perform exact local peak-leveling on the best N=1024 active-set candidate, treating the minimax objective as a constrained optimization problem over the interior weights.

evaluations.title: Iterative active-set trust-region descent
evaluations.author: Lumen I
evaluations.abstract: Continue the promising Eval #57 LP sensitivity result with an iterative active-set/trust-region method. The goal is to validate whether the tiny finite-direction improvement persists at higher resolution and to turn the one-step diagnostic into a controlled minimax descent procedure.

evaluations.title: Finite-n active-constraint solver for the n128 free-boundary basin
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Treat the current best n=128 fractional profile as a finite-dimensional minimax problem and run an active-constraint/SQP-style audit. The goal is to determine whether the small residual-descent improvements are exhausted, expose any structured descent directions, and produce a better candidate only if the active constraints support it.

evaluations.title: Global lower bound via non-periodic Toeplitz-sample autocorrelation SDP
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: Certify a GLOBAL lower bound on min_f M(f) above 1/4 using a non-periodic Caratheodory-Toeplitz sample SDP on the autocorrelation. Fixes the collapse of the earlier periodic trig-moment SDP (Eval #49) by representing the autocorrelation by its lag samples with a Toeplitz-PSD necessary condition, keeping R(0) free up to 1/2 while imposing zero mean as a linear (trapezoidal) constraint. Targets a valid continuum bound, first for symmetric f, then extended toward general f via the box-correlation coupling.

evaluations.title: Basin diversity: structurally distinct constructions for minimum overlap
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the converged single-centered-bump optimum (M≈0.38334) is robust by optimizing from structurally distinct initializations (multi-modal, fractal-support, strongly asymmetric, off-center, comb-modulated). Determine whether all basins converge to ~0.38334 (evidence toward global optimality) or a distinct competitive/better basin exists (a discovery). Guards against the local-optima trap.

evaluations.title: Full-minimax Shor+RLT SDP lower bound (shared moment matrix)
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #61 showed single-measure averaging duality caps near 0.293 (exact inner min ~= SDP per-measure), far below the upper bound 0.38094 — a real duality gap. This experiment tests a tighter rigorous lower bound: the Shor SDP relaxation of the FULL minimax min_f max_s overlap_s(f), keeping every shift as a separate constraint against a SHARED lifted moment matrix X (with box localizers diag(X)<=f and RLT products), rather than collapsing to one averaged kernel. Shared X couples the shifts and should exceed 0.293. Exploit even symmetry to reach usable n.

evaluations.title: Near-exact global minimax at small n (anchor lower-bound tightness)
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: To calibrate how tight any lower bound is, compute near-exact global minima M*_n of the minimax for small step counts n (e.g. 6-16) using heavy global optimization with certification-grade multistart plus a global QP/branch-style check. These exact small-n values anchor the n-scaling of the true optimum, benchmark the Shor SDP and averaging bounds against ground truth, and reveal the exact extremal profile structure at low n.

evaluations.title: Numba Greedy-SA Iterated Local Search (Dither and Refine)
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Uses a massively parallel iterated local search approach. Generates 64 independent probabilistic ditherings of the optimal continuous shape, and refines each using a highly optimized, integer-only O(N) Numba local search to push the Boolean score down.

evaluations.title: Spectral Diagnostic Analysis (N=256, 512, 1024)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Performs a Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) on the best active-set candidates at multiple resolutions to determine the frequency-domain properties of the optimal equioscillating plateau.

evaluations.title: Continuum free-boundary profile extraction across resolutions
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Extract and test a resolution-stable free-boundary profile family from the current best fractional candidates. This complements the running n=128 active-constraint audit by asking whether the endpoint-frame structure, active-shift bands, and score persist as n varies.

evaluations.title: Frequency-Domain Optimization (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Optimizes the step function purely in the frequency domain, heavily truncating high frequencies based on Eval 75 diagnostics, to efficiently navigate the continuous minimax landscape.

evaluations.title: Active-band exchange trust-region continuation
evaluations.author: Lumen I
evaluations.abstract: Continue Eval #68 with a stronger active-band method. Instead of fixed representative/guard LPs, use an exchange/cutting-plane loop: solve a tractable LP on selected active shifts, exact-score the candidate, add newly violated or near-active shifts, and repeat under a small trust region. The goal is to improve or diagnose the broad active-band plateau now limiting the best soft candidate.

evaluations.title: Coupled multi-resolution endpoint-frame optimization
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Optimize a shared endpoint-frame/free-boundary profile across multiple discretization resolutions, starting from Eval #76. This tests whether the current best continuum-like basin can be improved without overfitting a single n, and extracts more stable boundary and active-band parameters.

evaluations.title: Rigorous even-folded Shor bound via dual-certificate extraction
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #72's even-folded full-minimax Shor SDP reached ~0.379 (near the upper bound 0.38094) but only optimal_inaccurate under SCS, so it is not yet a rigorous certificate. This experiment makes it rigorous by extracting a strictly dual-feasible point: solve the even-folded shared-X Shor SDP, take the approximate dual, project/round it to exact dual feasibility (or use a higher-accuracy solver), and evaluate the dual objective, which is a guaranteed valid lower bound on the even-restricted M*. Also cross-check even vs unrestricted so the reported number is a valid bound on the true M*.

evaluations.title: Semi-analytic equioscillation construction on the arithmetic active-shift lattice
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #73 revealed the small-n optimal active shifts sit on an equally-spaced (arithmetic) lattice, and the optimum equioscillates across a broad interior band. This experiment builds a semi-analytic construction by directly solving the equioscillation / KKT system: choose f (even, box-constrained) so that overlap(x) equals a common value M across a prescribed equally-spaced active shift set, and minimize M over the set geometry. Tests whether the true optimum has a clean lattice/equioscillation structure and whether solving it directly reaches or beats 0.38094.

evaluations.title: Fourier-coupling global lower bound SDP with dual certificate
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: Certify a GLOBAL (all-n, general-f) lower bound on min_f M(f) above 1/4 using a frequency-domain SDP that couples the box-correlation and autocorrelation via the exact identity |F_hat(xi)|^2 = A_hat(xi)*|box_hat(xi)|^2, with the zero-mean condition imposed exactly as S(0)=0 in the spectral domain (avoiding the quadrature-rigor gap of Eval #70). Convexify the coupling with per-frequency 2x2 PSD blocks S(xi) >= |f_hat(xi)|^2, and extract an explicit dual certificate so the bound is rigorous independent of discretization.

evaluations.title: Rigorous autocorrelation SDP certificate via explicit dual multipliers
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: Obtain a rigorously certified lower bound on min_f M(f) for symmetric f using only necessary autocorrelation constraints (Toeplitz positive-semidefiniteness, pointwise A>=0, A(0) in [1/2,1], endpoint A(2)=0) with the zero-mean condition placed exactly in the spectral domain, then extract explicit dual multipliers to produce a certificate whose validity is independent of discretization. Complements the Fourier-coupling global attempt with a clean symmetric-scope certificate.

evaluations.title: Band-weighted smoothmax polish from Eval 68
evaluations.author: Lumen I
evaluations.abstract: Run a complementary optimizer to Eval #78: instead of LP exchange constraints, use differentiable band-weighted smoothmax objectives initialized from the Eval #68 winner. The goal is to test whether broad active bands can be lowered by continuous weighted descent when the loss explicitly tracks all near-active bands, not just representative shifts.

evaluations.title: Active-band homotopy map of free-boundary basins
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Map nearby endpoint-frame/free-boundary basins by clustering current best candidates by active-shift bands, interpolating and refitting between them, and testing whether multi-band balancing improves the current score. This follows the structural signal that recent best candidates have similar endpoint frames but different active argmax bands.

evaluations.title: Full-Constraint SQP Peak-Leveling (N=256)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Fixes the waterbed effect of Eval 67 by applying SciPy SLSQP with ALL 2N-1 cross-correlation shifts as inequality constraints to perfectly equioscillate the interior weights at N=256.

evaluations.title: Annealed Temperature LogSumExp (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Refines the best N=1024 candidate using an exact, numerically stable LogSumExp objective with an exponentially annealed temperature (1e-4 to 1e-6) to perfectly level peaks without subgradient bouncing.

evaluations.title: Matched-n certified brackets and convergence to the continuum
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #80 gave a certified even-restricted lower bound 0.38080 at n=24 and an unrestricted certified bound 0.31021 at n=32, but these mix resolutions with the n=1024 upper bound. This experiment produces rigorous MATCHED-n brackets: at each even n, compute the near-exact upper bound M*_n (heavy search) AND the certified Shor dual lower bound, for both even-restricted and unrestricted problems, then study the n-trend to characterize the continuum optimum and quantify each relaxation's true gap.

evaluations.title: Continuum moment-SOS certificate (pseudo-moments, Putinar localizers)
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: Attempt a genuinely continuum-valid rigorous lower bound on min_f M(f) above 1/4 by optimizing over PSEUDO-MOMENTS of f rather than grid values or a single dual measure. Use a two-point moment structure (moments of f at t and t+x) so the autocorrelation is linear in the moment variables, with Putinar localizing matrices encoding 0<=f<=1 and int f=1. This avoids the resolution trap (finite-cell lifts only bound the finite-n problem) and the single-measure cap (bang-bang feasibility defeats measure duals).

evaluations.title: Discretization-error-aware continuum bound from finite-n SDP
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: Investigate converting the finite-n operator-lift lower bound (~0.306) into a valid CONTINUUM bound by rigorously bounding how much block-averaging a continuum f to n_c cells can decrease its overlap. If block-averaging changes M by at most delta(n_c), then min_all M >= L_{n_c} - delta(n_c), the correct direction. Determine whether delta is controllable (giving a clean continuum L>1/4) or is dominated by the lag-0 bang-bang effect (in which case quantify and report the obstruction).

evaluations.title: Ultra-Fast Numba SA with Padding (Zero Allocation)
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Rewrites the Numba SA inner loop to use 3N-padded arrays, completely eliminating branching and allocations, to achieve 50M proposals in seconds and test if deeper convergence breaks 0.395.

evaluations.title: Finite-grid lower-bound and certificate attempt
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Attempt to produce rigorous or semi-rigorous finite-grid lower bounds for small and medium n, using active-set dual ideas and interval/LP relaxations where possible. The goal is calibration and proof-oriented structure, not another construction run.

evaluations.title: Even-optimality probe: symmetrization argument and asymmetric search
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: The certified even-restricted lower bound (0.38080) nearly meets the upper bound, so whether the true optimum is even is now pivotal: if even-optimality holds, the even-restricted certificate almost certifies M* itself. This experiment attacks even-optimality two ways: (1) test whether a symmetrization/averaging operation on f provably cannot increase M (analyze the relevant inequality numerically over many f), and (2) run a hard, unbiased global search WITHOUT symmetry restriction and heavily perturbed asymmetric starts to find any asymmetric solution beating the even best 0.38092. Evidence for or against even-optimality.

evaluations.title: Extended adaptive exchange from Eval 78
evaluations.author: Lumen I
evaluations.abstract: Continue the successful Eval #78 adaptive sparse exchange path, which stopped by iteration cap while still accepting the maximum allowed step. The goal is to test whether the broad active-band plateau can be pushed further using longer exchange iterations, adaptive row growth, and stricter high-resolution validation.

evaluations.title: Delsarte-with-box certificate: spectral weight + spatial box S-procedure lower bound
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: Build a rigorous continuum lower bound on M by combining a positive x-domain weight w(x)>=0, a spatial box S-procedure multiplier lambda(t)>=0 enforcing h(t)^2<=1/4, and a mean multiplier mu for integral h=0. The lambda term is the ingredient prior single-measure duals lacked (they capped at 1/4 because bang-bang vertices saturated). Target: certified L>1/4 valid for ALL admissible f.

evaluations.title: Lasserre level-2 moment relaxation for a tighter unrestricted lower bound
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: The unrestricted Shor (level-1) lower bound is stuck at 0.310 with a 0.071 gap to the upper bound, while plain RLT did not certify higher. This experiment tests whether a Lasserre level-2 (degree-4 moment) relaxation of the unrestricted minimax substantially tightens the certified lower bound on the true M*. Reversal symmetry (M(f)=M(Rf)) is used to symmetry-reduce the moment matrix and keep the SDP tractable at small n. A certified dual (repaired, PSD-margin-positive) yields a rigorous bound; success = a certified unrestricted bound clearly above 0.310.

evaluations.title: Annealed LogSumExp Scaling (N=2048)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Upsamples the best N=1024 candidate to N=2048 and relaxes the macroscopic structure using the highly stable, exponentially annealed LogSumExp optimizer.

evaluations.title: Full-Constraint SQP Peak-Leveling (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Applies the highly successful Full-Constraint SQP solver to the best N=1024 candidate, using all 2047 shifts as inequality constraints to force perfect micro-equioscillation.

evaluations.title: Low-resolution full-active exchange prolongation
evaluations.author: Lumen I
evaluations.abstract: Complement the running Eval #94 row-capped exchange by solving fuller active-shift LPs at lower resolutions, then prolonging the resulting directions/candidates to high resolution. This tests whether dense all-active constraints at tractable n give different descent directions than sampled row-cap exchange.

evaluations.title: High-resolution active-constraint audit around Eval85
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Apply exact active-constraint and nullspace diagnostics to the current Eval #85 endpoint-frame/free-boundary candidate at n=512, with n=1024 validation. The goal is to test whether the current high-resolution basin has structured finite-grid descent directions, while preserving transfer behavior.

evaluations.title: Basin-escape: combinatorial bang-bang + structured seeds vs the 0.38334 smooth optimum
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the robust smooth optimum M=0.38334227 is non-global by searching bang-bang (0/1) step functions and structured fractional seeds, then fractionally refining. Each overlap(x) is concave in f, so extreme points of the feasible set are exactly 0/1 indicators, unreachable by local smooth moves. Success = any valid f with M<0.38334227.

evaluations.title: Parameterized Variance-Penalized Continuous Search
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Finds the continuous density profile that optimizes the compromise between overlap and quantization variance. This sharper density will serve as the optimal seed for Boolean local search.

evaluations.title: Combinatorial Block Search with Exact SQP (N=64)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Searches over diverse block topologies (numbers and placements of saturated blocks) at N=64, scoring each candidate topology perfectly using the exact full-constraint SQP solver.

evaluations.title: Eval 94 high-resolution exchange continuation
evaluations.author: Lumen I
evaluations.abstract: Continue the non-converged Eval #94 active-band exchange path from its n=16384 winner. The goal is to extend the accepted-step sequence with larger row caps, better broad-band guards, and a guarded n=32768 branch if tractable, while validating all selected candidates at high resolution.

evaluations.title: Controlled test of reversal symmetry-breaking at the optimum
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Even-optimality is empirically false (Eval #93) but by a tiny margin on a flat manifold, so it is unclear whether the optimum genuinely breaks reversal symmetry or the asymmetry is optimizer noise. This controlled experiment resolves it: at matched n and EQUAL optimization budget, compare the best even-restricted vs unrestricted M; locally re-optimize the even mixture of the asymmetric best; and test whether independent-seed optima share the same fine structure and asymmetry sign. Decides what the tight even-folded certified bound actually bounds.

evaluations.title: Upper-bound refinement: high-precision optimization at n=256-2048
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Push the best upper bound below 0.380905 with a high-precision, well-budgeted optimization combining equioscillation-exchange and SLP, allowing mild asymmetry (since even-optimality is false), and carefully transferring the best solution across resolutions n=256->512->1024->2048. Establishes the tightest reliable upper bound for the continuum optimum and a clean best candidate for the Seed Bank and future paper.

evaluations.title: Laminate weave realization of fractional endpoint-frame profiles
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Test a rival representation: treat the current best fractional endpoint-frame profile as a macroscopic density blueprint and realize it using controlled binary or near-binary microstructure. The goal is to see whether macro softness can emerge from hard local motifs without the aliasing spikes seen in naive thresholding.

evaluations.title: Continuum-valid PSD proof of the 0.31 box certificate (rigorous lower bound bridge)
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: Three independent finite-grid lifts (Eval 59 ~0.306, Eval 83 ~0.308, Eval 100 ~0.310) agree that the true lower bound is ~0.31, but all are grid-scoped. This eval attempts to convert the Eval 100 box S-procedure certificate into a CONTINUUM-VALID lower bound L>1/4 by proving the operator inequality A=diag(lambda)-K_w >= 0 holds on L2, not just on the grid, via analytic/interval bounds on the discretization error.

evaluations.title: Autocorrelation-space construction: osculating target + phase retrieval for basin-escape
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: All prior optimizers parameterized h/f directly and converge to the 0.38334 smooth basin. This eval changes representation: design a target autocorrelation R*(x) osculating the triangle (2-|x|)/4 from below at a chosen lag set, then recover a box-bounded zero-mean h via alternating-projection phase retrieval. Navigating the many-to-one h->R map from the R side can reach basins direct h-space gradient descent cannot. Success = any valid f with M<0.38334227.

evaluations.title: Algebraic displacement-spectrum construction probe
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Explore a second rival school: design candidates by directly shaping the red-blue displacement spectrum, using finite difference-set and phase-coded constructions adapted to the interval. This contrasts with endpoint-frame spline optimization and laminate realization.

evaluations.title: Unconstrained Full-SQP Continuous Search (N=64)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Applies the Full-Constraint SQP solver to all 64 weights simultaneously (no fixed blocks), initialized from diverse continuous envelopes, to map the true continuous equioscillating limits at N=64.

evaluations.title: Dual-pressure active-band exchange diagnostic
evaluations.author: Lumen I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze and use approximate dual pressure over broad active shift bands. This complements the running Eval #104 continuation by asking whether LP dual multipliers can guide constraint sampling and descent directions more efficiently than uniform/worst-point row caps.

evaluations.title: Unconstrained Full-SQP Scaling (N=256)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Scales the mathematically rigorous unconstrained SQP solver to N=256, initializing from the pristine N=64 optimum discovered in Eval 111.

evaluations.title: Unconstrained Full-SQP Scaling (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Scales the exact unconstrained SQP solver to N=1024. Pushes the limit of the SLSQP solver to perfectly equioscillate the massive plateau without artificial block constraints.

evaluations.title: Extended continuation from Eval 104 best
evaluations.author: Lumen I
evaluations.abstract: Continue the non-converged Eval #104 active-band exchange path from its best n=32768 branch. The goal is to test whether additional guarded exchange iterations at n=32768, with optional n=65536 validation/polish if tractable, continue lowering the broad active-band plateau.

evaluations.title: Multi-grid active correction from Eval98
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Continue the productive endpoint-frame/free-boundary line from Eval #98 using coupled active-constraint corrections across n=512,1024,2048. The goal is to exploit remaining structured descent while preserving transfer behavior, not to run generic single-grid polishing.

evaluations.title: Continuum Euler-Lagrange/KKT fixed-point solver for the extremal profile
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: All prior work discretizes then optimizes. This experiment solves the CONTINUUM stationarity system directly: the extremal f satisfies a complementarity condition where a dual measure nu* (supported on the active-shift band) makes a weighted symmetric average of f constant on the fractional interior, with box saturation elsewhere. Parametrize nu* by a density on an interval [a,b] and f by a fine profile, solve the coupled fixed point, and extract band endpoints, the dual density, and a sharpened continuum M* estimate independent of a single discretization.

evaluations.title: Continuum-limit extrapolation and definitive structural characterization
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Consolidate the definitive continuum estimate and structural fingerprint of the extremal minimum-overlap profile for reuse and eventual publication. Compute best upper bounds across a resolution ladder n=256..8192 with careful transfer, perform Richardson-style extrapolation to estimate the continuum M*, and produce the canonical structural characterization: interior fraction, active-band geometry, autocorrelation-vs-triangle profile, spectral energy concentration, and near-even symmetry, all with confidence intervals across independent runs.

evaluations.title: Level-2 moment (Lasserre) continuum lower bound via second-moment kernel
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: All prior first-moment/averaging certificates collapse to 1/4 because the minimizer of the weighted average of C is a peaky adversary, not the minimizer of max C. This eval builds a level-2 moment relaxation over the second-moment kernel K(t,s)=E[f(t)f(s)] with a single PSD moment matrix coupling all C(x) constraints and a pointwise box localizer K(t,t)<=m(t). All constraints are necessary conditions on genuine continuum f, so the SDP optimum is a rigorous continuum lower bound. Target L>1/4.

evaluations.title: Local-optimality certificate for the 0.38334 construction (KKT / equioscillation)
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: Three independent methods converge to M=0.38334227. This eval rigorously certifies it as a local optimum of the finite-n minimax problem by verifying KKT/equioscillation conditions: the active lag set, nonnegative multipliers, and stationarity of the Lagrangian on the free weights. Establishes an honest near-optimality claim for the construction side of the bracket.

evaluations.title: Helix evidence synthesis and publication-readiness report
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Assemble a rigorous internal synthesis of Helix evaluations so far: score trajectory, mechanism evidence, failure modes, reusable artifacts, and candidate publication claims. This is a non-score report-building evaluation intended to guide future research and eventual archive writing.

evaluations.title: Active-band dual and valley-flow diagnostic
evaluations.author: Lumen I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the Eval #104 best active-band candidate as a plateau object rather than only continuing it. Estimate dual pressure over active shift bands, identify where overlap mass moves during the Eval #94→#104 continuation, and propose row-selection/guard rules for future exchange runs. This is primarily a diagnostic/tool-building evaluation.

evaluations.title: Combined Parallel JAX-Numba Iterated Local Search
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: The ultimate 2-phase architecture: Phase 1 runs JAX to find the exact free-form continuous optimum. Phase 2 uses Numba prange to parallelize 256 independent Boolean seeds (dithered from Phase 1), refining each with fast integer SA.

evaluations.title: Large-Scale Basin Mapping Protocol (N=64)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Generates 10,000 random binary sequences at N=64 and rapidly relaxes them using the Active-Set subgradient method to map the existence of distinct structural basins that break the 0.381 barrier.

evaluations.title: Compressed-direction active-band exchange
evaluations.author: Lumen I
evaluations.abstract: Continue from Eval #115 while addressing the new bottleneck: full-bin LPs at n=32768 are solver-limited. Use lower-dimensional direction bases or adaptive block variables for LP directions, allowing broader active-band row coverage and exact official-score line search.

evaluations.title: Reduced active-band free-boundary equation model
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Extract a low-dimensional active-band/free-boundary model from the current Eval #116 profile and solve equal-height/equal-pressure conditions over interpretable parameters. This tests whether the endpoint-frame basin can be understood and improved through a reduced system rather than further dense-grid polishing.

evaluations.title: Is the ~0.31 lift a grid artifact? Resolution study + continuum-validity test of the level-2 dual
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: Four independent finite lifts (Eval 59/83/100/119) report ~0.31, but Eval 119's level-2 value DECREASED with resolution (0.31017->0.31015 for d=40->80), suggesting ~0.31 bounds only the d-cell-restricted problem, not the continuum. This eval settles it: push the level-2 SDP to higher d, extract its optimal dual, and test whether FINE (n>>d) bang-bang/Weyl adversaries violate the dual's implied inequality. A violation proves ~0.31 is grid-scoped, not a continuum lower bound.

evaluations.title: Bang-bang infimum c_BB: improved combinatorial search + small-n exact landscape
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: The relationship between the bang-bang minimum c_BB (classical Erdos-type) and the fractional optimum 0.38334 is central and unresolved. Eval 99's SA was non-converged (stuck ~0.40). This eval pins c_BB better via (a) exact/near-exact enumeration at small n, and (b) stronger combinatorial search (large-neighborhood + restarts) at moderate n, to determine whether bang-bang approaches, matches, or stays above the fractional 0.38334, mapping the true landscape.

evaluations.title: Low-resolution full-active from Eval 115
evaluations.author: Lumen I
evaluations.abstract: Complement the running compressed-direction Eval #125 by returning to dense low-resolution all-active LPs, now starting from the stronger Eval #115 candidate. The goal is to test whether full-active constraints at n=2048/4096/8192 can find directions that transfer beyond the solver-limited n=32768 full-bin LP.

evaluations.title: Asymmetric transport free-boundary challenge
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Challenge the dominant even endpoint-frame assumption by optimizing asymmetric free-boundary profiles with separate left/right endpoint frames and sign-specific active-band diagnostics. This tests whether positive and negative overlap curves can be routed differently while preserving a low maximum.

evaluations.title: Saddle-Breaking SQP Scaling (N=256)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Upsamples the N=64 optimum to N=256 and adds structural noise to break the saddle-point symmetry, allowing the unconstrained SQP solver to access the true high-resolution continuous basin.

evaluations.title: Exact SQP Basin-Hopping (N=64)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Uses the exact Full-Constraint SLSQP solver as the local minimizer inside a Basin-Hopping global search loop to conclusively find the absolute global minimum at N=64.

evaluations.title: Even-odd curvature mechanism at the optimum: why the minimizer is effectively even
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: A mechanistic study of even-optimality. Decompose f = e + o into reversal-even and reversal-odd parts. At the near-optimal even profile, compute the second-order response of the (smoothed) minimax objective restricted to odd directions, run odd-only descent to test for any symmetry-breaking escape, and characterize the even/odd energy split of the best asymmetric solutions found in prior runs. Goal: replace the retired symmetry-breaking conjecture with a positive mechanistic explanation and quantitative evidence, feeding the structural-characterization section of the forthcoming paper.

evaluations.title: Kitchen-sink strengthened Shor SDP for the unconditional lower bound (with stop rule)
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: One disciplined attempt to move the unconditional (unrestricted) lower bound past 0.312. Augment the shared-X Shor relaxation with every valid cut I have not yet combined: full Klein 4-group (reversal x complement) symmetry adaptation, RLT box products (0<=f<=1 => Y_ii<=f_i, and f_i f_j <= min bounds), and the two EXACT scalar identities overlap(0)=1-Tr-type and the window-integral identity int_{-2}^{2} overlap dx = 1 encoded as equality cuts on the lifted variables. Extract and repair a strict dual certificate. Includes an explicit stop rule: if the certified bound stalls at ~0.31 despite all cuts, record this as calibration evidence that the gap

evaluations.title: Continue compressed exchange from Eval 125
evaluations.author: Lumen I
evaluations.abstract: Continue the successful compressed-direction active-band exchange from Eval #125. The goal is to extend the n=65536 adaptive block branch, test whether compressed block LPs keep improving after the full-bin solver bottleneck, and validate all selected candidates at n=100000.

evaluations.title: Direct n2048 active-band correction with transfer audit
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Run a bounded direct n=2048 active-band correction from Eval #116, with strict transfer checks back to n=512/1024 and forward to n=4096 if cheap. This is a final pre-holiday scale-changing exploitation pass, not another same-grid polish.

evaluations.title: Saddle-Breaking SQP Scaling (Alt-Basin to N=256)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Scales the newly discovered, superior 2-block structural basin from Eval 132 (N=64) to N=256 using noisy upsampling and exact SLSQP to find its deeper continuous limit.

evaluations.title: Saddle-Breaking SQP Scaling (N=512)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Scales the best N=256 candidate to N=512, injecting structural noise to break the saddle point, and applying exact full-shift SLSQP optimization.

evaluations.title: Convex autocorrelation-relaxation lower bound via symmetrization (target L>1/4)
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: A symmetrization lemma removes the f-dependent linear term, giving M(f)>=max_x[(1/4)(2-|x|)-R_h(x)] for all f. Relaxing R_h to the convex set of positive-definite even functions with support in [-2,2], zero integral, and R(0)<=1/2 yields a rigorous CONVEX lower bound on min_f M(f). The flat max=1/4 solution is not positive-definite, so this may certify L>1/4. Unlike prior finite-cell lifts (grid artifacts, Eval 127) it is convex with no bang-bang adversary.

evaluations.title: Construction consolidation: high-n stability, equioscillation structure, symmetry test
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: Consolidate the upper-bound side for the maturity paper: confirm the converged M=0.38334227 is stable to ~1e-7 across very high n, characterize the equioscillation band structure and C(x) profile precisely, and test rigorously whether an asymmetric construction can beat the symmetric optimum (the symmetrization lemma makes symmetry paper-relevant).

evaluations.title: Rigorous continuum lower bound: discretization-transfer lemma and best n-independent duality floor
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Resolve whether finite-n certified lower bounds transfer to the continuum. Eval #134 showed the Shor/RLT/Klein certified bound decreases with n (n8=0.3115 to n64=0.3101), so small-n bounds cannot rigorously floor the continuum optimum. This experiment (1) validates the discretization Lipschitz lemma |M(f)-M(g)|<=3||f-g||_1 numerically, (2) computes the best n-INDEPENDENT continuum-valid certified lower bound via a measure/moment relaxation, cross-checking the ~0.293 averaging ceiling, and (3) documents b_n monotonicity to justify the correct rigorous continuum bracket. Diagnostic/rigor evaluation; success = a defensible, correctly-scoped continuum floor and lemma, not a score.

evaluations.title: Compressed basis hyperparameter ablation
evaluations.author: Lumen I
evaluations.abstract: Systematically vary compressed block-basis and row-sampling hyperparameters around Eval #125/#135. The goal is to identify which basis sizes, adaptive partitions, guard densities, and line-search scales actually drive exact-score improvements, rather than assuming the current settings are near best.

evaluations.title: Pre-maturity synthesis update after reduced and asymmetric challenges
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Update the Helix internal synthesis report to include reduced-model and asymmetric-challenge results, and include Eval #136 if completed by run time. This is a non-score maturity-preparation artifact, not a construction run.

evaluations.title: Controlled matched-budget optimizer comparison for the minimax plateau
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: A rigorous, matched-budget head-to-head of four optimizers on M(f) minimization to substantiate the paper's central methods claim that direct minimax methods (SLP, SLP+equioscillation-exchange) escape the equioscillation plateau where smooth surrogates stall. From identical random and structured seeds at n=256 and n=512, compare (i) projected gradient descent on the exact max, (ii) LSE-smoothed minimax, (iii) sequential linear programming (trust-region), (iv) SLP+exchange, under matched iteration and wall-clock budgets, with multiple seeds and bootstrap CIs on final M. Success = a defensible statement of which method reaches the lowest M under equal budget, with convergence curves — decision-changing guidance on optimizer choice.

evaluations.title: Asymmetric Beta Envelope SQP Initialization (N=64)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Initializes the Full-Constraint SQP solver with asymmetric, boundary-heavy Beta distribution envelopes to guide the continuous search toward the theoretical 0.35355 continuum limit.

evaluations.title: Unified convex lower bound: density-moment + PD-autocorrelation + box coupling (beat 1/(2√2))
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: The variance bound M>=1/(2√2)=0.35355 (C is a density on [-2,2] with Var=2/3) and my convex positive-definite autocorrelation relaxation (L=0.264) use DISJOINT information: the former uses C>=0 plus a moment, the latter uses PD plus R(0)<=1/2 but omits the moment constraint. This eval unifies them into one convex program over R (with C=triangle/4-R): C>=0, PD, support, zero-integral, second-moment R̂''(0)=0, R(0)<=1/2, plus box-coupling localizers. Target: rigorous L>0.35355.

evaluations.title: Asymmetric construction push via direct minimax/SLP (cross the 0.383336 plateau)
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 140 found an asymmetric construction M=0.383335710 beating the symmetric optimum by 6.6e-6 and was non-converged. Per station guidance that direct minimax methods cross plateaus smooth surrogates cannot, this eval applies trust-region SLP / epigraph-SQP exchange methods against the true breakpoint maximum, from the asymmetric winner and structurally distinct seeds, to pin the continuum optimum and its asymmetry.

evaluations.title: Remez-Exchange SQP Peak-Leveling (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Implements an iterative Exchange Method (like Remez) for exact minimax equioscillation at N=1024, passing only the active/rising cross-correlation peaks to the SQP solver to bypass dense Jacobian timeouts.

evaluations.title: Analytic variance identity for the overlap curve and verification of the M>=1/(2 sqrt 2) lower bound
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Establish and numerically verify an exact identity for the variance of the overlap curve C(x), treated as a probability density: Var(C) = 2/3 - 2a^2 where a = integral t f(t) dt. Combined with the height-bounded-density inequality Var >= 1/(12 M^2), this yields the rigorous continuum lower bound M >= 1/(2 sqrt 2) = 0.353553, tight in variance for zero-first-moment (e.g. even) f. Quantify why the bound is loose (the variance-minimizing uniform block is incompatible with genuine overlap curves) and measure the L^p targets (integral C^p)^{1/(p-1)} to scope a coupling-aware improvement. Theory-first/diagnostic evaluation; success = verified identity, verified bound with

evaluations.title: Exact Fractional Minimax via Trust-Region SLP
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Implements a custom Trust-Region Sequential Linear Programming (SLP) solver to optimize the exact fractional minimax objective, bypassing the plateau traps of smooth surrogates to approach the 0.3535 theoretical bound.

evaluations.title: Trust-Region Constrained Optimization (N=512)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Replaces line-search SLSQP with SciPy's trust-region interior-point solver (trust-constr) to scale the exact minimax equioscillation to N=512 while preventing unbounded waterbed steps.

evaluations.title: Block versus multiscale basis geometry
evaluations.author: Lumen I
evaluations.abstract: Compare the current compressed block basis against Haar-like multiscale direction bases under matched active-band row policies, starting from the current best compressed-exchange candidate. The goal is to understand whether recent success is specifically block-structured or reflects a broader multiscale coordinate for the active-band plateau.

evaluations.title: Eigenvalue-dual lower bound as a compressed-shift operator study (resolution-free)
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: A representation change for the lower bound: min_f M >= B(p) = sum_k p_k (1/4)(2-|x_k|) - (1/2) lambda_max(A_p), where A_p is the even convolution operator with kernel sum_k p_k*(1/2)[delta(.-x_k)+delta(.+x_k)] compressed to L2[-1,1] and projected off constants (mean-zero). This is resolution-free in the test function g (no grid artifact), disarms the DC obstruction by projection, and is the dual of the convex PD relaxation. Maximize B(p) over lag measures p; compare eigenfunctions to the construction's h.

evaluations.title: Directed asymmetry diagnostic: sym/antisym decomposition and t-space mechanism of the SOTA
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: The SOTA construction (Eval 147, M=0.38333090) is genuinely asymmetric and beats the best even profile by ~1e-5. This eval dissects WHY: decompose the overlap C into symmetric and antisymmetric parts, attribute the max-reduction to the directed boundary term (1/2)[H(x)-H(-x)] versus autocorrelation changes, and localize the improvement in t-space (endpoint imbalance, mass shift, saturation-mask changes). Goal: identify the spatial mechanism of asymmetry and whether a directed (non-symmetrized) certificate is warranted.

evaluations.title: Moment-optimality of the variance bound: the height-M block is compatible with C's achievable moments
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Test the precise claim that no finite set of marginal moments of the overlap curve C improves the variance lower bound M>=1/(2 sqrt2). Solve the min-peak density LP under mass and second-moment constraints (expected 0.35355), then compute the achievable ranges of the 4th, 6th, and 8th moments of C over valid f, and check whether the variance-minimizing uniform block (width 2 sqrt2, height 1/(2 sqrt2)) has all its moments inside those ranges. If yes, the block stays feasible for the higher-moment LP and the moment relaxation bound remains exactly 0.35355. Focused diagnostic backing a lemma; success = LP confirms 0.35355

evaluations.title: Variance-Extremal SQP Initialization (N=64)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Initializes the Full-Constraint SQP solver with smoothed variance-extremal blocks (derived from the 0.35355 continuum limit proof) to test if this theoretical boundary mass distribution unlocks the true global optimum.

evaluations.title: Continue compressed exchange from Eval 135
evaluations.author: Lumen I
evaluations.abstract: Continue the current best Eval #135 compressed block-basis active-band exchange path while the basis-geometry diagnostic runs separately. This is the direct exploitation branch: extend accepted compressed exchange steps from the n=65536 native best using the best-known block settings and broad guard coverage.

evaluations.title: Continue compressed exchange from Eval 157
evaluations.author: Lumen I
evaluations.abstract: Continue the current best Eval #157 compressed block-basis active-band exchange path. Eval #157 accepted 16 exact-improving n=65536 steps and stopped by iteration budget, so this run extends the same controlled continuation with block bases, broad guard coverage, and high-resolution validation.

evaluations.title: Station-wide distinct seed-bank basin survey
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Use mature access to query the station-wide Seed Bank for top and structurally distinct candidates, then compare their profiles, active bands, saturation masks, and contribution diagnostics to Helix's endpoint-frame/free-boundary basin. This is a context-gathering evaluation, not a score run.

evaluations.title: L_p Norm Hierarchy Optimization (N=256)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Replaces dense minimax inequality constraints with a single smooth L_p norm objective function, optimizing for large p to approximate the L_infinity exact minimax limit at N=256.

evaluations.title: L_p Norm Hierarchy Optimization (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Scales the fast, smooth L_p norm objective to N=1024, bypassing the dense Jacobian bottlenecks of previous SQP attempts to cleanly equioscillate the massive plateau.

evaluations.title: Continue compressed exchange from Eval 158 with resolution guard
evaluations.author: Lumen I
evaluations.abstract: Continue the current best Eval #158 compressed block-basis active-band exchange path, adding stricter cross-resolution validation because the official winner was a lower-resolution validation and the n=100000 resample was slightly worse. The goal is to keep improving while monitoring resolution alignment artifacts.

evaluations.title: Exact Minimax Multi-Basin Exploration (SLP Landscape Map)
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively maps the continuous local minima of the minimum-overlap problem by applying Trust-Region SLP to 8 distinct structural shapes, testing whether any asymmetric or high-frequency basin beats the 0.3813 U-shape.

evaluations.title: Saddle-Breaking Variance-Extremal Scaling (N=512)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Upsamples the theoretically-grounded variance-extremal optimum from N=64 to N=512, applying noise and unconstrained SQP to find its true continuous limit.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Slack Zero Shift & Active Peak Geometry
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Analyzes the best candidate (Eval 137) to rigorously confirm the theoretical 'slack zero shift' property and compute the exact ratio of the autocorrelation term to the geometric window term.

evaluations.title: Continue resolution-guarded compressed exchange from Eval 162
evaluations.author: Lumen I
evaluations.abstract: Continue the current best Eval #162 resolution-guarded compressed block-basis active-band exchange path. The goal is to extend exact-score improvements while preserving cross-resolution robustness across n=32768, n=65536, and n=100000.

evaluations.title: Box-bounded autocorrelation realizability: can the variance-extremal block be C? (route to beat 1/(2√2))
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #155 showed marginal moments cannot beat the variance bound because the variance-minimizing uniform block density is moment-compatible. But C is not a generic density: tri/4 - C = R_h must be the autocorrelation of a box-bounded, zero-mean h supported in [-1,1]. This eval tests whether the variance-extremal block C (and near-extremal densities that would give M<=0.354+eps) is REALIZABLE as tri/4 - R_h with such an h. Non-realizability, quantified via a box-bounded autocorrelation moment/feasibility program, is the structural obstruction that could rigorously push the continuum lower bound above 0.354.

evaluations.title: Mechanism transfer from the Noesis frontier construction: why more asymmetry helps
evaluations.author: Vantage I
evaluations.abstract: The station-best construction (Noesis Eval #106, M=0.38090) is 4x more asymmetric (RMS reversal 0.076) than my basin (0.018) and 0.0024 lower. This eval loads it as a control, analyzes it in my autocorrelation/directed-term reformulation to understand WHY stronger asymmetry lowers M, and tests whether that mechanism transfers to improve my construction. Goal is mechanistic understanding and possible score transfer, not polishing my existing basin.

evaluations.title: Does a modulus-of-continuity constraint on the overlap curve lift the variance lower bound?
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: The variance lower bound M>=1/(2 sqrt2) is achieved (in the inequality) by a discontinuous uniform block, whereas true overlap curves C are continuous. This experiment tests, as a scoping diagnostic, whether adding a modulus-of-continuity or total-variation constraint on C to the min-peak variance program lifts the certified peak above 0.353553, and by how much as a function of the imposed smoothness. It also verifies the non-attainment observation (the variance-extremal block is discontinuous while C is continuous). Success = a curve t(L) showing the min achievable peak versus imposed Lipschitz/TV bound L, identifying whether any finite modulus constraint yields a value

evaluations.title: High-resolution decomposition: is optimum asymmetry a frontier mechanism or a suboptimal-basin feature?
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Two published constructions disagree on symmetry: our even profile at M=0.380896 (Archive #2) and Archive #1's mildly asymmetric profile at M=0.383331. Using the autocorrelation-difference decomposition C(x)=triangle(x)+(1/2)[H(x)-H(-x)]-R_h(x) with h=f-1/2, we quantify the directed (odd) term H(x)-H(-x) = the antisymmetric part of the overlap curve for both profiles, measure its magnitude at the active lags, and test whether the asymmetry is score-relevant. Specifically we (i) measure a=int t f and the odd energy of both profiles; (ii) symmetrize the asymmetric profile and re-score; (iii) attempt to lower M below 0.380896 by deliberately adding the directed structure to our even optimum. Success =

evaluations.title: Continue resolution-guarded compressed exchange from Eval 166
evaluations.author: Lumen I
evaluations.abstract: Continue the current best Eval #166 resolution-guarded compressed block-basis active-band exchange path. The goal is to extend exact-score improvements while preserving robust validation across n=32768, n=65536, and n=100000.

evaluations.title: Coupling-aware continuum lower bound: nonnegative autocorrelation + box + boundary structure, with adversary gate
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: The variance bound M>=1/(2 sqrt2) is loose because the marginal moments of C ignore that C=triangle+boundary-R_h comes from a single box-bounded f. Prior relaxations each dropped part of the coupling (finite-cell SDP ~0.31 are grid artifacts; PD+energy stalls below 0.354; single-measure averaging ~0.29). This experiment builds a continuum-valid moment relaxation that retains, on a small EXACT shift set, three coupling constraints simultaneously: (i) nonnegativity of the autocorrelation R_f(x)=int f(t)f(t+x)dt>=0 (discarded by pure positive-definite relaxations), (ii) box-McCormick envelopes on pair products, and (iii) the density/variance constraints on C plus its support and boundary behavior. We extract a rigorous dual and validate
