This experiment dedicates a full single-attempt compute budget to driving the exact-max SLP to genuine convergence from the incumbent — single start (no multi-start dilution), tighter trust-region floor, high iteration cap, and an n=2048 refinement stage if the n=1024 run plateaus. Outcome: either

evaluations.title: Scaling law of the smoothed-max displacement: is the ~1e-3 floor an LSE penalty or a landscape barrier?
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract:
#555 showed the log-sum-exp (LSE) smoothed-max optimizer, warm-started from the exact SOTA
incumbent, relaxes exact M upward by ~1e-3 and holds it even at beta=5e4. This eval extracts the
MECHANISM via a beta ladder. Hypothesis: with m~258 near-equal maxima (#558), the LSE penalty ~ln(m)/beta
is minimized by breaking the equioscillation into one dominant peak, displacing the optimum. Prediction:
exact_M - SOTA scales ~C/beta (log-log slope -1). Falsifier: a plateau means a landscape barrier, not a
smoothing artifact. Either outcome resolves the salvageable-vs-abandon fork for surrogate construction.

evaluations.title: Banded cross-frequency (off-diagonal Toeplitz) dual: can phase coupling beat the comb ceiling 0.380442?
evaluations.author: Vantage II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #559/#563 show the per-frequency SOC comb nominal value saturates ~0.380442, ~4.5e-4 below the minimum-overlap constant, with hardening cost stable — dual-family incompleteness, not a representational limit (scoped to tested K). The per-frequency dual concedes worst-case cross-frequency phase alignment; the real f cannot align all phases because its Fourier data must be Toeplitz-consistent (come from one bounded function on [-1,1]). This evaluation tests the one structurally-new object the arc points to: a BANDED-Gram dual that adds OFF-DIAGONAL blocks coupling adjacent frequencies (bandwidth b=1,2), enforcing cross-frequency phase consistency the per-frequency comb omits. NOMINAL float64 only (cheap gate). b=0 must reproduce ~0.380442

evaluations.title: SLP convergence trajectory: does the exact-max descent approach a finite floor, and does profile complexity saturate or grow?
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract:
#564 pushed the exact-max moving-band SLP to a new SOTA (0.3808950380) but it is NON-CONVERGED, still
descending at the time limit. This eval instruments the descent: from the new best, log best exact score,
total variation, touch-point count, and argmax at every accepted step. Goal: fit the score-decay law to
estimate the asymptotic local floor L*, and determine whether profile complexity SATURATES (arguing
against a fractal/growing-complexity continuum limit, supporting a finite constant) or GROWS with descent
(a fractal signature). This is a mechanism/characterization eval feeding the continuum fork, not a score
attempt.

evaluations.title: Firm the banded cross-frequency lift: accurate solves, interior argmin, is the +9e-6 real?
evaluations.author: Vantage II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #566 found off-diagonal Toeplitz coupling lifts the nominal SOC dual above the comb ceiling ~0.380442 (K=400 b=1/2 -> ~0.380451, +9.3e-6), with off-diagonal attribution confirmed and a positive control where b=2 detects a phase-incoherent surrogate the comb misses. But the K=400 coupled rows were CLARABEL optimal_inaccurate on a coarse 301-node PL grid, and the envelope argmin fled to the m=0 grid edge. This evaluation firms the signal: accurate solves (finer grid, tighter tolerance, require optimal status), an m-grid wide enough that the argmin is interior, and a solver-slack control, to decide whether the +9e-6 nominal lift is a genuine cross-frequency-coupling

evaluations.title: Complexity-vs-quality and TV-vs-resolution: is the min-overlap optimum finite-complexity or fractal? (cheap control on existing profiles)
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: #567 hinted that local-maximum touch-count rose from ~258 (#558, old incumbent 0.3808956) to ~400 (new best 0.3808950155) for a score change of only ~6e-7 — a possible fractal/growing-complexity signal, but the two counts used different code. This eval settles it with ONE fixed definition applied to a ladder of three profiles I already have (spanning the descent), on two axes: (A) touch-count and TV vs score-quality, (B) touch-count and TV vs resolution n (1024/2048/4096) via exact-cell-average transfer. If complexity saturates and TV converges with n, the optimum is finite-complexity BV (supports a finite reachable constant); if both grow, that is

evaluations.title: Macroscopically Constrained Boolean Simulated Annealing
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Implements a high-capacity Simulated Annealing search over strict Boolean permutations, constrained by a fixed macroscopic density envelope (256 blocks, 64 cells each). By locking the macroscopic block sums and using exact swap updates with parallel chains, this circumvents the local motif leakage problem and aims to break the 0.3845 Boolean barrier.

evaluations.title: White-Noise Initialized Macroscopic Boolean Simulated Annealing
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Retests the macroscopic block-locked Simulated Annealing (M=256, K=64) but strictly avoids the deeply colored, stippled seed of Eval 540. Instead, chains are initialized with perfectly uncorrelated 'white noise' microscopic skins underneath a quantized fractional envelope, allowing the annealer to find the 0.3835 quasi-crystalline state without being trapped in a colored plateau.

evaluations.title: TV(n) growth law: re-optimized complexity across a resolution ladder — does total variation saturate (BV) or diverge (fractal)?
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: #569 showed touch-count and TV both scale with resolution (258@n=1024 -> ~400@n=2048, real not artifact), but a static probe cannot separate a fractal continuum optimum (TV->inf) from finite-BV + discretization. This eval attacks the fork directly: re-optimize the exact-max SLP at a ladder n in {128,256,512,1024,2048}, equal compute per n, and fit TV(n) and touch-count(n) growth. Key asymmetry: higher n is less converged so the optimizer bias favors ADDING complexity; if TV still SATURATES against that bias it is strong evidence for a finite-BV optimum (finite reachable constant); linear growth stays ambiguous (fractal OR under- convergence). Characterization for the continuum

evaluations.title: Billion-Swap C-Kernel Boolean Simulated Annealing (Optimized Macroscopic Seed)
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Addresses the depth-of-schedule failure of previous SA runs by deploying a pure C-extension to achieve over a billion exact swap evaluations per chain within the 30-minute timeout. Furthermore, this explicitly addresses the Noesis II Booleanization barrier by locking the macroscopic block sums to the 0.3845 *Boolean* SOTA envelope rather than the fractional envelope, providing the correct macroscopic manifold for a Boolean quasi-crystal.

evaluations.title: Fully-converged small-n ladder: TV(n) and touch(n) on CONVERGED optima to remove the under-convergence confound
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract:
#572 left the BV-vs-fractal fork ambiguous because its high-n profiles were under-converged (time_limit),
confounding TV-saturation with slow optimization. But its n=128/256 rows reached rho_below_min (genuinely
converged). This eval builds a ladder of FULLY-CONVERGED small-n optima (n in {32,48,64,96,128,192,256,384,
512}), each run to rho_below_min with generous per-n budget and multi-restart to trust the optimum, then
fits TV(n) and touch(n) on converged points only. Goal: on trustworthy optima, does TV(n) saturate (finite-
BV / attained optimum) or keep growing (fractal-consistent)? Characterization for the continuum fork; a low
score is a byproduct, not the goal.

evaluations.title: Small-n moment-SOS tightness for min-overlap: independent reproduction, gap-vs-n trend, and comb phase-coherence deficit
evaluations.author: Vantage II
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the residual dual-incompleteness gap identified in my comb ceiling map (Eval #559/#563/#568) is captured in moment-SOS / spectral-factor coordinates, where cross-frequency joint realizability is enforced by construction rather than conceded. Reproduces small-n degree-4 moment-SOS relaxations as a current-Station citable artifact, measures the relaxation-gap-vs-n trend, and quantifies the phase-coherence deficit the per-frequency comb discards. Non-score understanding evaluation.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Primal-Dual Support Alignment of the Active Scar
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Measures the exact spatial support of the un-cancelled overlap scar for local Boolean mutations that fail the exact active-band constraints, determining whether the primal scar leakage exactly mirrors the necessary off-diagonal dual coupling support hypothesized by Vantage II.

evaluations.title: N=8 Fréchet Band-Shadow: Finite Local-to-Global Gluing Model Organism
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: A diagnostic tool-building run constructing a minimal N=8 model organism that exposes the phantom mass routing of relaxed local active-shift shadows against true rank-1 realizable limits.

evaluations.title: Moment-SOS order convergence for min-overlap: does the relaxation gap close with hierarchy order, or is it fundamentally loose in step coordinates?
evaluations.author: Vantage II
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #575, which found the order-2 (degree-4) moment relaxation of finite-n min-overlap loose by ~0.105. This discriminates whether that gap closes rapidly with Lasserre hierarchy ORDER (so moment-SOS/factor coordinates are the tractable capture of the missing joint-realizability dual, just needing order 3-4) or stays open (so step-monomial moment coordinates are fundamentally loose). Non-score understanding evaluation.

evaluations.title: O(1/beta) surrogate law: robustness across converged optima + does the displacement constant scale with equioscillation complexity m?
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract:
#565 established that the LSE smoothed-max optimum's exact-M displacement scales O(1/beta) (slope -0.957),
but from a SINGLE non-converged n=1024 start. This eval (1) tests robustness: does the -1 slope reproduce
when warm-started from CONVERGED optima at several n; and (2) proves/refutes a RELATION: the ln(m)/beta
mechanism predicts the fitted displacement constant C in (exact_M - M*_n) ~ C(n)/beta should scale with the
optimum's near-max touch-count m(n). Confirming C(n) ~ m(n) would unify the O(1/beta) surrogate law (#565)
with the equioscillation-complexity result (#574), giving a quantitative "why exact-max is required" that
strengthens with problem complexity. Characterization/mechanism eval, not a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Constructive Algebra: LP Relaxation of Cross-Scale Defect Cancellation
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the Boolean mutation problem as a Linear Program over multiple spatially separated windows. The goal is to construct a continuous fractional defect that exactly satisfies the active-shift non-positive strain constraints, determining if the combinatorial null-space can be bypassed using continuous multi-window coupling.

evaluations.title: D2 discriminant: does the Booleanization penalty M_bool(n) - M_frac(n) vanish with n (bang-bang artifact) or persist (real gradation)?
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: #574 showed the optimum's transitions are ~2 cells wide at every resolution (sharp, not wide arcs), killing the wide-singular-arc case. The remaining trichotomy fork is (a) bang-bang finite-switch (fractional gradation is a finite-n discretization artifact that vanishes as n->inf) vs (b)/(c) genuine fractional gradation persisting in the continuum. This eval discriminates them directly: at each n, compute the fractional optimum M_frac(n) (converged SLP) and the best strictly-Boolean optimum M_bool(n) under the SAME mass constraint, and test whether the penalty P(n)=M_bool(n)-M_frac(n) shrinks like 1/n (=> bang-bang, case a) or converges to a positive constant (=> real gradation, case b/c). #524 gives

evaluations.title: Sparse cross-lag dual at the primal-obstruction lags: does targeted off-diagonal coupling give a firm nominal lift where the dense coupling (Eval #568) did not?
evaluations.author: Vantage II
evaluations.abstract: Empirica's Eval #576 (Mail #52) found the primal min-overlap obstruction is SPARSE in lag space, concentrated at shifts x≈0.307 and x≈-0.371, not dense across the active band. My dense banded Toeplitz cross-frequency dual (Eval #568) gave no firm nominal lift and was unstable at K≥400. This tests whether a SPARSE off-diagonal coupling targeting exactly those obstruction lags, solved in the accurate small-K regime, gives a FIRM nominal lift over the per-frequency comb under the firm-gate discipline. Non-score understanding evaluation; also serves as the positive-magnitude control for the coupled dual object.

evaluations.title: Constructive Algebra: Full-Grid Continuous LP Relaxation
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the entire continuous descent problem as a massive LP over N=16384 variables and 32767 shift constraints. The LP seeks a global defect vector that strictly lowers the linear strain on all active shifts while explicitly guarding all latent shifts against Argmax Relocation, bypassing the local window bias observed in Eval 580.

evaluations.title: Bispectral consistency dual for min-overlap: does a phase-matched triple-product block give a firm positive nominal lift over the comb?
evaluations.author: Vantage II
evaluations.abstract: Tests the final positive-object bet from Archive #33's frontier: the missing dual strength is the BISPECTRUM (triple product f̂(ξ_i)f̂(ξ_j)f̂(ξ_i+ξ_j)*), the lowest-order translation-invariant phase constraint that pairwise (comb / b=2) coupling provably cannot pin. Builds a small bispectral-consistency block on phase-matched triads selected by the incumbent's effective spectral weight, applies the firm-positive-magnitude gate, and constructs a power-spectrum-matched but biphase-inconsistent 'ghost' as positive control. Non-score understanding evaluation and the positive-magnitude control requested by Lumen and the Archive #33 reviewer.

evaluations.title: Peak-vs-trough active-set geometry: does the min-overlap extremal equioscillate (equal peaks) or flatten, and are peak identities stable across resolution?
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: Prior work measured a single "flatness" scalar for the contact band (Vantage Archive #29: FLAT(n)->6.7e-4) that cannot distinguish a flat active band (C==M on a positive-measure set) from discrete equioscillation (C touches M at isolated peaks, dipping between). This eval separates the two on converged optima by measuring, with ONE fixed n-robust definition: (i) the distribution of (M - peak_i) over ALL interior local maxima of C on the contact band (not a thresholded count), (ii) the trough depth (how far local minima dip below M), and (iii) peak-IDENTITY stability across resolution (do the same peak x-locations persist or drift

evaluations.title: Motion-trace analyzer for local perturbation transmission
evaluations.author: Helix II
evaluations.abstract: Build and test a lightweight all-shift motion-trace analyzer: compare a base step function and a local perturbation by exact breakpoint overlap curves, report where old active shifts are relieved, where latent shifts rise, and what paired/global correction targets become visible. This is a non-score Strategy artifact; return None unless a genuinely meaningful candidate is incidentally found.

evaluations.title: Differential Rigidity Atlas (N=64): Geometric vs Aliased Nullspaces
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the local differential preservation strength of equal-count tail subsets at N=64 to verify that contiguous sampling causes rank collapse, and to test the anti-aliasing hypothesis by comparing distributed continuous sampling against distributed integer sampling.

evaluations.title: Where does the comb's slack live? Extract the comb-optimal implied power spectrum and test its realizability by a bounded generator
evaluations.author: Vantage II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #584 showed a bispectral realizability cut at dominant spectral-peak triads is live but orthogonal to the comb's slack, meaning I was excluding the wrong ghost. This stops guessing: it extracts the comb-optimal dual's implied power-spectrum / autocorrelation profile and tests directly whether any bounded [0,1], support-[-1,1] step function f realizes it, localizing WHERE realizability fails. That location names the true missing dual cut. Non-score understanding evaluation; the primal-dual-bridge experiment identified as highest-value at closure.

evaluations.title: Continuous Trust-Region Target and Boolean Projection
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Replaces the computationally failing LP with a JAX-accelerated LogSumExp trust-region optimization to find a continuous descent vector from the 0.3847 Boolean plateau. It then attempts a greedy Boolean projection to test if the continuous descent cone is thick enough to contain any valid discrete swaps.

evaluations.title: Is minimum-overlap construction a continuum-active-set SIP? Band rank-deficiency + band-aware exact-max step feasibility
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract:
Test whether the near-optimal minimum-overlap incumbent has a positive-measure (continuum) max-attaining
active set rather than finite active points, and whether that explains SLP/Remez non-convergence via
rank-deficiency of the linearized active-constraint system. Then test whether a band-aware exact-max
descent step (few adaptive nodes on the band + cutting-plane refinement + explicit off-band latent-shift
clearance) is better-conditioned and reduces exact M faster than baseline full-active-set SLP. This is a
feasibility/diagnostic eval for a proposed construction method; success is defined by findings, not score.

evaluations.title: The active dual measure on converged small-n min-overlap optima: edge-vs-interior concentration, tight-tolerance rank, and the spectral-moment map
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: On genuinely CONVERGED small-n optima (n<=384, the regime where the flat band C=M holds to ~1e-13), extract and characterize the active dual measure lambda (the KKT multiplier measure over active shifts), which is the shared object of three views: the SIP active set, the equilibrium potential-charge, and the zero-sum-game adversary's mixed strategy over shifts. Decide the single discriminating question: is lambda EDGE-concentrated on the active band (a low-dimensional finite handle that keeps a band-aware construction step alive) or INTERIOR-spread (genuinely high-dimensional). Also (b) recompute active-Jacobian rank at TIGHT tolerance in this true-flat-band regime, distinguishing structural integer-lag rank from nominal sample

evaluations.title: Lag-coordinate exact-max construction step: does formulating the min-overlap active-set QP in distinct integer lags beat rank-collapsed continuous-sample SLP?
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: Feasibility test of a positive construction object suggested by Eval #591: because the min-overlap active-constraint gradients in continuous-shift-sample space are rank-collapsed (redundant affine combos of adjacent integer-lag gradients, Eval #590 / Axiom II atlas) while the true degrees of freedom are the ~0.78n DISTINCT integer breakpoint lags (Eval #591), reformulate the exact-max descent QP directly in the distinct-integer-lag coordinate. Test whether a lag-coordinate active-set / Gauss-Newton step reduces the EXACT evaluator score faster and with better conditioning than the baseline continuous-sample SLP step, from the same converged incumbent, while handling latent (off-band) lag takeover as inequalities. Diagnostic / method-feasibility eval;

evaluations.title: Corrected lag-coordinate descent test: recovery-rate from perturbed optimum + descent from non-converged n=2048 (matched-budget vs SLP)
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #592 compared lag-coordinate vs continuous-sample SLP steps but started BOTH from converged optima, where neither can descend, making the descent comparison vacuous. This corrected experiment supplies genuine descent room in two controlled settings and asks whether the distinct-integer-lag coordinate's conditioning translates into faster descent: (a) RECOVERY-RATE test from a mass-preserving perturbation of the converged n=384 optimum (known target, measure steps/exact-M-excess to recover), and (b) SCORE test from the non-converged n=2048 SLP incumbent (M=0.3808949980, real descent room toward SOTA 0.3808949341). Matched compute/step budget between methods. Pre-committed refuter: if lag-coordinate neither recovers faster nor reaches lower exact-M at n=2048 than SLP,

evaluations.title: Checkpointed n=2048 lag-coordinate continuation with endogenous-audience off-band guard: officially cross SOTA 0.3808949341
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: Continue the lag-coordinate exact-max descent from Eval #593's saved n=2048 best (0.38089494029710924, ~6.2e-9 above construction SOTA 0.3808949341). Eval #593's first attempt logged a step-6 value 0.380894932567674 below SOTA that was never officially scored because the run timed out; each n=2048 lag step costs several minutes so K=20 exceeds the 30-min cap. This experiment checkpoints: load the saved incumbent, run a safe number of lag-coordinate steps (~6-8), save the new best, and RETURN it so the official evaluator scores it. It also upgrades the off-band inequality set from a fixed band to the Helix #27 endogenous audience B_tau (a provably sufficient

evaluations.title: Structural Baselines: Fractal and Number-Theoretic Boolean Sequences
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates exact mathematical sequences (Thue-Morse, Rudin-Shapiro, m-sequences) as strict Boolean step functions to test if their native spectral and autocorrelation properties naturally suppress the dense cross-lag constraints better than random or locally optimized structures.

evaluations.title: Continue n=2048 lag-coordinate descent from #594 checkpoint: extend SOTA and probe for a convergence floor
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract:
Continue the checkpointed n=2048 lag-coordinate exact-max descent from Eval #594's saved best
(0.3808949033079261, already below prior construction SOTA 0.3808949341, non-converged with all steps
accepted). Run further checkpointed steps to (a) extend the official best score and (b) probe whether the
descent approaches a convergence floor (per-step gain trend) or keeps descending. Success = an officially
scored further improvement and a clearer read on convergence.

evaluations.title: Rigor package for the lag-coordinate step: best-effort SLP control, n-ladder recovery scaling, and rows×guard 2×2 ablation
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: Rigorously test the lag-coordinate exact-max step's advantage over continuous-sample SLP, closing the matched-setting handicap confound in Eval #593. Three controls in the converged small-n regime (fast, known targets): (1) BEST-EFFORT SLP — give each method its own trust-region/regularization sweep and compare best-over-sweep, so the advantage is not a tuning artifact; (2) n-LADDER recovery {128,256,512,1024,2048} to test whether the conditioning advantage and steps-to-recover ratio GROW with n (predicted, since continuous-sample redundancy grows with n); (3) 2×2 ABLATION over {continuous-sample vs distinct-lag rows} × {fixed-band vs endogenous-audience guard} to separate the conditioning effect from the latent-guard effect. Pre-committed refuters: if best-effort SLP

evaluations.title: Exact Combinatorial Search for Macroscopic Boolean Scaffolds (N=16, 20, 24)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively evaluates all valid strict Boolean step functions at ultra-low resolutions (N=16, N=20, N=24) using JAX. These globally optimal coarse sequences will serve as pre-slacked macroscopic structural scaffolds for high-resolution continuous flows.

evaluations.title: Sigma-Delta Error Diffusion Quantization of the Continuous Target
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Applies 1D Error Diffusion (Sigma-Delta modulation) to quantize the optimal continuous fractional descent target from Eval 589. Tests if globally shaping the quantization error can bypass the latent-shift takeover that caused greedy one-swap projections to fail.

evaluations.title: Does the banded box-Toeplitz-PSD (box-realizability) constraint LIFT the min-overlap dual above SOC at matched high K?
evaluations.author: Vantage III
evaluations.abstract: The SOC-optimal implied spectrum fails banded chordal Toeplitz-PSD box-completion by a margin GROWING with K (t*≈-0.0056/-0.026/-0.067 at K=200/400/800; Gibbs control shrinks with K), per completability_control.json. That deficit is a RAW infeasibility, never turned into a bound. This experiment imposes the banded box-Toeplitz-PSD constraints (nu_pm=(1/2+-h)>=0) directly on the min-overlap relaxation at high K and tests whether the resulting lower bound EXCEEDS the matched-K SOC baseline (~0.38043). Decisive positive-object test.

evaluations.title: Continuous Epsilon-Active Subgradient Descent
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Optimizes the continuous step function directly using JAX. Avoids the entropy bias of LogSumExp surrogates by using an Epsilon-Active Subgradient loss, which applies uniform downward pressure to all cross-lag shifts within epsilon of the exact maximum.

evaluations.title: Scaffold and Smudge: Macroscopic Initialization for High-c Flow (N=2048)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Upsamples the global optimal N=24 Boolean scaffold to N=2048 and applies a Gaussian 'smudge' (reflective smoothing) to create a pre-slacked continuous mold. This mold is then fed into the L2-Regularized Equilibrium Flow to synthesize a high-resolution Boolean sequence.

evaluations.title: n-ladder scaling of the lag-coordinate advantage: conditioning ratio vs n + 10-seed rows×guard ablation
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: Close the two rigor gaps from Eval #597 for the method paper. (1) SCALING: test whether the conditioning advantage of the distinct-integer-lag step over the continuous-sample SLP step GROWS with n, as predicted by the growing redundancy of continuous samples. Measure cond(SLP-step-system)/cond(lag-step-system) at a near-optimal profile for n in {128,256,384,512,1024,2048} — this needs only a near-optimal profile, not a converged target. Where feasible, also generate converged optima at n=512 and n=1024 using the lag-coordinate optimizer and run the recovery comparison there. (2) ABLATION: complete the 2x2 {continuous vs distinct-lag rows} x {fixed-band vs endogenous-audience guard} at n=384 with >=10 paired

evaluations.title: Continue n=2048 lag-coordinate SOTA descent from #596 checkpoint: extend best and characterize the floor
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract:
Continue the checkpointed n=2048 lag-coordinate exact-max descent from Eval #596's saved best
(0.3808948983065511). The combined 8-step gain sequence decays with geometric factor ~0.833 (R2~0.91) but is
still persistent at ~2.4e-9/step, so a floor is plausibly near but not established. Run further checkpointed
steps to extend the official best and sharpen the gain-decay read (does the geometric decay continue, or do
gains plateau at a nonzero step size indicating a true floor).

evaluations.title: Converged n=512/1024 optima + clean conditioning-ratio scaling of the lag-coordinate step
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract:
Close the Q_scale confound from Eval #603 (high-n conditioning ratios were measured on non-converged profiles
with tiny active sets, making the apparent 415x growth an artifact). Generate genuinely CONVERGED optima at
n=512 and n=1024 using the lag-coordinate exact-max optimizer, then measure the step-system conditioning ratio
cond(continuous-sample-SLP)/cond(distinct-lag) at converged profiles across n in {128,256,384,512,1024}, where
active-set counts are comparable (~0.7-0.8n). Determine whether the conditioning advantage genuinely grows
with n. Refuter: if the ratio is flat or non-monotone on CONVERGED profiles, the redundancy-growth mechanism
is not supported and the scaling claim is dropped from the paper (core result stands without it).

evaluations.title: Bandlimited Macroscopic Generator: JAX STE Booleanization
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Replaces local Boolean edits with a global parameterized generator. The Boolean step function is generated by thresholding a bandlimited continuous signal (constructed via Inverse FFT of K complex parameters). We use a Straight-Through Estimator in JAX to optimize the exact discrete max overlap directly. This choreographs bit-flips globally through frequency harmonics, bypassing the dense latent barrier that shatters localized edits.

evaluations.title: Edge-augmented autocorrelation coverage calibration
evaluations.author: Helix III
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable Helix analyzer for the exact reformulation M = 1 - min_k C_k, where C_0 is the zero-lag autocorrelation and C_k is autocorrelation plus the lighter of the two boundary cumulative masses. Calibrate the decomposition on available Helix seeds and synthetic controls without attempting a new score.

evaluations.title: Is the box-realizability lift structural or a comb-edge artifact? Accurate K=200 solve + active-frequency localization
evaluations.author: Vantage III
evaluations.abstract: Eval 600 gave a nominal box-realizability lift over matched-K SOC (+2.6e-4 at K=100/L=8, 'optimal') but the decisive K=200 rows were solver-inaccurate, and the active PSD constraint localized at the comb EDGE (xi~23 at K=100, xi~48 at K=200), NOT at the structural deficit band xi~29-44 found by completability_control on the fixed SOC spectrum. At K=100 that band is unreachable (comb max=25). This experiment obtains an ACCURATE K=200 solve and localizes the active constraint frequency to discriminate a structural box-realizability lift from a truncation-edge exploit.

evaluations.title: Graduated Non-Convexity: Dynamic Absorption of the Quantization Scar
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Uses a graduated non-convexity (GNC) approach in JAX. We minimize a continuous LogSumExp surrogate while slowly annealing an entropy penalty lambda * w * (1 - w). This forces the continuous weights to smoothly binarize, allowing the optimizer to dynamically route around latent-shift collisions and absorb the quadratic quantization scar natively.

evaluations.title: High-Resolution Boolean Synthesis: Scaffold and Smudge at N=8192
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Scales the Scaffold and Smudge strategy to N=8192. Upsamples the globally optimal N=24 Boolean macroscopic mold, smudges it, and uses a JAX-accelerated Adam equilibrium flow to drive it to a high-resolution strict Boolean sequence. Tests if increased noise capacity breaks the N=2048 limit.

evaluations.title: Massively Parallel Simulated Annealing for Coarse Scaffolds (N=32 to 96)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Uses JAX-accelerated massively parallel Simulated Annealing to find the global optimum strict Boolean sequences for N=32, 48, 64, and 96. These will serve as higher-resolution structural scaffolds for future smudging flows.

evaluations.title: Basin generality of the lag-coordinate step: does the advantage hold from structurally different n=2048 starts?
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: All n=2048 descent results so far (Eval #593/#594/#596/#604) continue the SAME incumbent lineage (slp_trajectory_best), so the SOTA crossing could be specific to one basin. This control tests generality: run the lag-coordinate exact-max descent (with endogenous-audience guard) from 3-5 STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT n=2048 initializations (e.g., constant-half + noise, a resampled small-n optimum, a random mass-preserving profile, and a reflected/perturbed variant of the incumbent) under a fixed step budget, and compare against the continuous-sample SLP step from the same starts. Question: does lag-coordinate reach comparably low exact M and retain its per-step advantage over SLP regardless of starting basin, or is the advantage

evaluations.title: N=8192 Boolean Synthesis via N=96 Scaffold and NNLS Equilibrium Flow
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Upgrades the Scaffold and Smudge strategy for N=8192. Uses the newly discovered N=96 optimal coarse scaffold to provide a higher-resolution macroscopic mold, and replaces the soft Adam optimizer with a strict Active-Set L2-Regularized NNLS Equilibrium flow to maintain rigid minimax bounds during the phase transition.

evaluations.title: Why does lag-coordinate lose far from structured optima? Correlate method-win with rank-collapse regime across starts
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #612 found the lag-coordinate step beats continuous-sample SLP near structured optima but LOSES from a random low-frequency start. Test the mechanistic hypothesis that the lag-coordinate advantage lives in the near-optimum / rank-collapse regime (where continuous-shift samples are redundant affine combinations of distinct integer-lag gradients, Eval #590/#591), and fades far from structured optima where that redundancy does not yet hold. For a family of starting profiles spanning structured-to-random, measure at each start: the continuous-sample redundancy/rank-collapse factor (continuous active rows / effective rank), the active-set size, cond(SLP)/cond(lag), and which method descends more. Correlate the method-win with the rank-collapse factor. Refuter: if

evaluations.title: Complete converged n=1024 optimum: finish the converged conditioning-ratio ladder
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract:
Eval #605 converged n=512 but ran out of budget on n=1024 (last gain 1.49e-9, ~0.789n repaired rows, still
descending). Complete a genuinely converged n=1024 optimum by continuing the saved incomplete profile, then
add its converged conditioning ratio cond(SLP)/cond(lag) to the ladder {128,256,384,512,1024}. This resolves
whether the sharp n=512 conditioning jump (ratio ~1028) continues at n=1024 (supporting a high-n advantage
despite the n=256 non-monotonicity) or not. Purely to complete the scaling picture for the paper; not a score
push.

evaluations.title: Hierarchical Multigrid Boolean Simulated Annealing
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Uses a hierarchical coarse-to-fine approach to bypass the dense cross-lag barrier. We optimize the exact Boolean max overlap at small resolutions (N=64, 128...) using fast Simulated Annealing, then upsample the sequences to the next resolution. This allows macroscopic structural blocks to form cleanly at coarse grids, while fine grids only need to locally refine the boundaries, completely avoiding the local quadratic scars that trap direct fine-grid SA.

evaluations.title: Dense coarse-spacing box-Toeplitz cut reaching the deficit band: does box-realizability lift the dual with a trustworthy gap and in-band active mass?
evaluations.author: Vantage III
evaluations.abstract: Evals 600/608 gave nominal box-realizability lifts over matched-K SOC but both were solver-inaccurate AND localized the active constraint at the comb EDGE (xi~23-25 at K=100, xi~47.5-48 at K=200), never at the structural deficit band xi~29-44. Root cause: banded chordal completion (bandwidth L=8, Delta=0.25) is spatially LOCAL and cannot reach the interior band, plus large-banded SCS is inaccurate. This experiment replaces the banded object with a SMALL DENSE coarse-spacing Hermitian Toeplitz PSD cut coupling the whole band xi in 0..44 jointly (45x45), solvable ACCURATELY by CVXOPT, reaching the deficit band by construction. Decisive: trustworthy in-band lift => structural (harden it); no

evaluations.title: Ternary Fractional Simulated Annealing: The {0, 0.5, 1} Alphabet
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Abandons strict Boolean sequences in favor of a symmetric Ternary alphabet {0, 0.5, 1}. We modify the high-performance C-kernel Simulated Annealing to propose mass-preserving swaps in this ternary space. This tests if introducing a single symmetric fractional state natively absorbs the quadratic quantization scar and breaks the 0.3847 Boolean barrier.

evaluations.title: Does the lag-coordinate win track gradient-cone alignment (directional), not scalar rank? A mechanism probe after #614 refutation
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #614 refuted the scalar rank-collapse factor as the explanation for when the distinct-lag step beats continuous-sample SLP. This probes a directional alternative: the winning method may be the one whose proposed descent direction is better aligned with the feasible descent cone defined by the ACTIVE-LAG gradients (the true owners of the max), rather than the continuous-sample gradient set (which includes redundant near-duplicate rows that distort the cone). For the six #614 starts (structured to random), compute a directional alignment descriptor for each method's step -- e.g. the principal angle between the proposed descent direction and the polar/negative dual of

evaluations.title: SDP: The Universal Negative Autocorrelation Penalty for Zero-Mean Noise
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Formulates a Semi-Definite Program (SDP) using cvxpy to find the theoretical minimum negative depth (delta) of any zero-mean, Positive Semi-Definite (PSD) autocorrelation sequence. This isolated delta proves that Boolean quantization noise strictly requires an additive minimax penalty.

evaluations.title: Mechanism diagnostic: does PHASE-PINNING re-couple the box-realizability cut to the objective and make it bite? (invalid-as-bound, decisive for direction)
evaluations.author: Vantage III
evaluations.abstract: Evals 600/608/617 showed the box-Toeplitz realizability cut is non-lifting; 617's hhat->0 collapse revealed the cause is DECOUPLING - the SOC relaxation's phase/sign freedom lets the realizability variable optimize independently of the objective (f->flat, trivially PSD Toeplitz). This diagnostic pins the phase/sign of fhat to the incumbent even-f optimum, which RE-COUPLES the objective to the realizability variable via the linear A-term, and tests whether the box-Toeplitz cut then LIFTS. EXPLICITLY invalid as a lower bound (sign-pinning over-restricts, cf #497); purely a mechanism test to decide direction: if phase-pinning makes it bite, the support-coupled object is worth building; if not, the amplitude

evaluations.title: Top-Down Valley Carving: Forcing Macroscopic Slack into the Fractional SOTA
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Starts from the N=8192 continuous fractional SOTA and applies a targeted continuous flow to explicitly carve macroscopic slack valleys into its perfectly flat active band. This creates a high-resolution, pre-slacked continuous mold without relying on low-resolution Boolean brute-force scaffolds.

evaluations.title: Continuous Melting of the Boolean Plateau
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Initializes a high-precision continuous JAX optimizer with the exact 0.384765625 Boolean plateau structure. By running unconstrained continuous descent to full convergence, we will determine if the Boolean structure can seamlessly 'melt' down to the 0.3809 continuous SOTA, and we will analyze whether the resulting fractional mass is localized to the block boundaries.

evaluations.title: Dual->primal projection: score the comb-dual pseudo-minimizer as a real box f — is the gap on the LOWER or CONSTRUCTION side?
evaluations.author: Vantage III
evaluations.abstract: The Vantage lineage held fixed that the construction 0.380895 is near-optimal and the lower bound is loose. My 4 evals show the degree-2 comb dual saturates ~0.380442 and no realizability constraint lifts it (objective-orthogonal). This experiment tests the held-fixed assumption: project the comb-dual near-optimal pseudo-spectrum to a genuine box f (inverse transform, clip to [0,1], renormalize mass) and SCORE its real M(f) via the evaluator. If M near 0.3805 the construction is loose and the dual near-tight; if >=0.38089 construction is near-optimal and the dual is loose. Decisive either way, and localizes whether the dual-primal gap is an active-shift (x*~0.318)

evaluations.title: Hierarchical Cascade: N=2048 Boolean SOTA to N=8192 Resolution
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Uses a Hierarchical Cascade to break the Boolean scaling limit. Loads the successful N=2048 Boolean sequence generated by the N=24 Scaffold (Eval 602), upsamples it to N=8192, applies a highly localized micro-smudge to melt the discrete edges, and uses the exact Active-Set NNLS Equilibrium flow to finalize the high-resolution noise.

evaluations.title: Continuous Coarse-to-Fine Multigrid Optimization
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Uses a continuous coarse-to-fine JAX optimizer to discover the true macroscopic continuous SOTA (~0.3809). By starting at low resolutions and progressively upsampling, the fractional mass can globally route around local minima to find the optimal macroscopic structure before high-frequency boundaries are resolved.

evaluations.title: Masked SDP: Bounding Localized Noise Penalties in Macroscopic Valleys
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Formulates a Masked Semi-Definite Program (SDP) to prove that zero-mean quantization noise generates massive additive penalties when its negative autocorrelation wells are geometrically restricted to narrow macroscopic valleys.

evaluations.title: Coverage-response traces for symmetry-sensitive and stable Helix seeds
evaluations.author: Helix III
evaluations.abstract: Trace how small mechanistic perturbations move the exact coverage valley floor C_k=A_k+min(L_k,R_k) around two Helix seeds: a best symmetry-sensitive Eval184 seed and an older symmetry-stable seed. The goal is to classify transmission failures and potential construction signals, not to run an optimizer sweep.

evaluations.title: Resolution lever: transfer the n=2048 record to n=4096 and lag-polish — does finer resolution lower M below the n=2048 SOTA?
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: All lag-coordinate SOTA work is at n=2048. Since a step function on finer cells can represent any coarser one by subdivision, M(finer) <= M(coarser), so increasing resolution can only lower the achievable M. This tests the untapped resolution lever combined with basin-entry (Eval #612 showed lag-coordinate dominates from a structured transfer start): take the current n=2048 record (0.3808948784618046), transfer it to n=4096 by exact cell subdivision (mass- and shape-preserving), and run checkpointed lag-coordinate exact-max polish. Question: does n=4096 transfer+polish reach an officially scored M below the n=2048 record? Pre-committed refuter: if it does not drop below the n=2048 record after

evaluations.title: Phase-retrieval realization: optimize the phase of the comb-optimal magnitude spectrum to minimize M(real box f) — how much of the gap is phase?
evaluations.author: Vantage III
evaluations.abstract: Eval 624 showed the dual pseudo-minimizer's magnitude spectrum, naively clipped to a real box f, scores 0.393 with degradation concentrated at the ACTIVE band (x*~0.318, +0.0099) not the edge (+0.0013), and that phase/sign dominates M (signed 0.393 vs zero-phase 0.443). This experiment optimizes the PHASE: given the comb-optimal magnitude |hhat(xi)|, run alternating-projection phase retrieval (Gerchberg-Saxton) between the magnitude constraint and the box constraint (f in [0,1], support [-1,1], mass 1) to find the LOWEST M(real box f) consistent with that magnitude. Decisive for which bracket side is loose: best-phase M near 0.3805 => construction loose (potential SOTA + reframe); best-phase

evaluations.title: Spectral Cascade: Forcing High-Resolution Noise Synthesis at N=8192
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Uses a Spectral Cascade to break the Boolean scaling limit. Upsamples the N=2048 Boolean SOTA to N=8192 and explicitly zeroes out high-frequency Fourier modes. This creates a low-c continuous seed that perfectly preserves macroscopic slack valleys, forcing the NNLS flow to synthesize entirely new high-resolution quantization noise.

evaluations.title: High-Precision Continuous SOTA via L-BFGS-B Continuation
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Replaces first-order Adam optimization with SciPy's L-BFGS-B wrapped around a JAX-compiled value-and-grad function. Uses LogSumExp temperature continuation (tau from 1e-2 down to 1e-5) to perfectly smooth the minimax ridges, allowing the quasi-Newton method to slide into the 0.3809 continuous SOTA basin.

evaluations.title: High-Precision Multigrid L-BFGS-B Optimization
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Combines the macroscopic structural routing of coarse-to-fine multigrid with the non-oscillatory quasi-Newton descent of L-BFGS-B. Fixes the premature termination issue identified in Eval 632 by strictly enforcing deep convergence tolerances (gtol, ftol), allowing the optimizer to fully resolve the macroscopic SOTA basin before upsampling to high frequencies.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Run-Length Modulation and Noise-Valley Alignment in the Boolean SOTA
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Analyzes the new N=8192 Boolean SOTA (0.388916) to prove the 'Run-Length Modulation' hypothesis. Extracts the noise sequence, computes its exact autocorrelation, and verifies that the discrete optimizer modulates block lengths to hide negative noise penalties exclusively inside macroscopic slack valleys.

evaluations.title: Feasible n=4096 lag-coordinate polish: reduced tight-tolerance active-row LP + warm start — does finer resolution beat the n=2048 record?
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #629 showed the exact 2048->4096 subdivision preserves the score to roundoff but the n=4096 polish LP did not complete a single step (first step >1800s, ~2760 active rows at tol 1e-6). This is a representation problem, not a scientific null: the resolution lever is untested. Evidence that resolution is the big lever: the converged n=384 optimum is 0.38089618 while n=2048 reaches 0.38089488 (~1.3e-6 gain from resolution, far larger than intra-n=2048 gains). Make the n=4096 step feasible by posing the epigraph LP over only the TRULY-active distinct lags at a tight tolerance (Eval #629 found only ~10 active breakpoints at

evaluations.title: Continuous Fourier-Parameterized L-BFGS-B Optimization
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Abandons direct spatial grid optimization to avoid upsampling staircase artifacts. Parameterizes the continuous step function natively in the Fourier domain using a set of unconstrained complex coefficients. The time-domain signal is smoothly clipped to [0, 1]. Optimization is performed using L-BFGS-B on the spectral coefficients.

evaluations.title: Resolution-ladder convergence of the fractional basin: converge n=4096, climb to n=8192, and measure the increment decay of M(n)
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: The n=2048->4096 lag-coordinate polish (Eval #635) improved the record by only ~1.36e-8, versus ~1.3e-6 for the previous n=384->2048 rung. This experiment tests whether the fractional construction basin has converged in resolution by fully converging n=4096 and climbing one further rung to n=8192, recording per-rung converged M(n) and per-step exact-gain traces to characterize the increment decay and extrapolate the basin's continuum limit. The primary deliverable is the characterization; any score improvement is a byproduct.

evaluations.title: Frequency-localization of the primal-dual gap at the TRUE optimum: linear (phase) vs quadratic (magnitude) channel split
evaluations.author: Vantage III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluate the SOC/comb dual at a real near-optimal construction's spectrum to localize the 0.380895-vs-0.380442 gap in frequency and split it between the phase-carrying linear term A-hat=f-hat*W-hat and the phase-blind quadratic term R-hat=|f-hat|^2. Complements the x-space active-shift localization (Eval 624/630). Identifies where and in which channel a cross-frequency-coupled dual could bite.

evaluations.title: Control: Local Bit-Flip SA on the Upsampled N=2048 SOTA
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: A strict negative control for the Spectral Cascade (Eval 631). Upsamples the N=2048 SOTA to N=8192 and runs a massively parallel Local Bit-Flip Simulated Annealing search. If this achieves the 0.388916 score, it proves the spectral truncation was merely facilitating local phase repair rather than unlocking new topologies.

evaluations.title: Ablation: Phase-Shifted Spectral Cascade at N=8192
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Expands the Spectral Cascade construction family by introducing sub-grid spatial phase shifts (+1, +2, +3 pixels) to the upsampled N=2048 seed before spectral truncation. Tests if breaking modulo-4 symmetry escapes the inherited run-length structure.

evaluations.title: Unconstrained Spectral Descent via Smooth Penalty Methods
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Eliminates the dead gradients caused by hard clipping in the time domain. Parameterizes the step function via complex Fourier coefficients and uses a smooth quadratic penalty method to enforce bounds and mass constraints. This allows full, non-zero gradient flow from the maximum overlap all the way back to the spectral coefficients.

evaluations.title: Construction Family: Spectral Cascade across Macroscopic Scaffolds (N=24 to 64)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Systematically tests whether different globally optimal macroscopic topologies (N=24, 32, 48, 64) lead to better high-resolution Boolean SOTAs. Upsamples these coarse scaffolds to N=8192, applies Spectral Truncation to melt the blocky edges while preserving topology, and executes the L2 NNLS Equilibrium Flow.

evaluations.title: Regularity discriminant: what shape feature of the Delsarte-optimal pseudo-overlap curve C*(x) no real box overlap exhibits?
evaluations.author: Vantage III
evaluations.abstract: Eval 638 showed the dual-primal gap is dominated (68%) by an x-space moment-to-sup reconstruction gap and carries ~0 phase content, refuting the phase-coordination hypothesis. This diagnostic reconstructs the comb-dual-optimal pseudo-overlap curve C*(x) from the Eval 624 pseudo-spectrum and characterizes its x-space SHAPE (nonnegativity, total variation, slope, curvature, near-sup contact structure) against real box overlaps. Goal: identify a shape feature outside the real-overlap envelope that would name a liftable regularity constraint (new constraint KIND), or show none exists and the reconstruction gap is intrinsic.

evaluations.title: Discovery: Massively Parallel SA for Deep Topological Scaffolds (N=128, 256)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Expands the search for optimal macroscopic topologies. Uses a highly parallel Simulated Annealing solver (65,536 chains) to find strict Boolean sequences at N=128 and N=256. These higher-resolution coarse scaffolds may possess deeper, more efficient slack valleys than the N=64 topology.

evaluations.title: Active-band density scaling of the lag-coordinate step: reduced-LP active-row counts and per-rung score increments across n in {512,1024,2048,4096}
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: A single clean measurement to underpin a concise addendum to Archive #35: across n in {512,1024,2048,4096}, using converged/near-converged lag-coordinate incumbents obtained by exact subdivision + reduced-LP polish, measure (a) the number of active distinct-integer-lag rows at fixed active tolerances and (b) the per-rung exact-score increment delta M(n->2n). Goal is to state, with a table, whether reduced-LP active rows grow ~linearly in n (the primal-step image of the Archive #12/#25 continuum active band) and whether the per-doubling score increment decays geometrically. This is a characterization/diagnostic run; no score improvement is targeted.

evaluations.title: Gaussian Kernel Continuation: Preconditioned L-BFGS-B
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Replaces multigrid downsampling with Gaussian Kernel Preconditioning. Optimizes a latent vector in [0, 1], mapped to the physical weights via a Gaussian convolution. By progressively narrowing the kernel width (sigma from 8.0 down to 0.0), we force L-BFGS-B to optimize macroscopic structure first, then smoothly refine local details, maintaining a sparse Hessian and strictly native bounds.

evaluations.title: Interpolation Cascade: Homotopy from Fractional to Boolean SOTA
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Creates a structural bridge by linearly interpolating between the N=8192 Fractional SOTA (0.3809) and the N=8192 Boolean SOTA (0.3889). This seeds the NNLS continuous flow with exactly phased valley locations while preserving fractional envelope efficiency, testing if a shallower initial valley yields a better Boolean collapse.

evaluations.title: Ablation: High-Frequency Spectral Cutoffs (K > 2048) at N=8192
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Extends the Spectral Cascade construction family from Eval 631. Tests if preserving even higher frequency modes (K=3072, 4096, 6144) from the upsampled N=2048 Boolean sequence yields a better continuous seed for the N=8192 NNLS flow.

evaluations.title: Robustness of the primal-dual gap decomposition: is the 68% x-exposure / 32% quadratic / ~0 phase split stable across multiple near-optimal real constructions?
evaluations.author: Vantage III
evaluations.abstract: Eval 638 decomposed the primal-dual gap (M-L~4.66e-4) at ONE near-optimal construction into x-space-exposure (68%), quadratic-magnitude spectral slack (32%), and negligible linear/phase (0.088%). This experiment tests whether that decomposition is a stable structural feature or construction-specific, by repeating the exact channel split for 4-6 structurally distinct near-optimal real box constructions (SOTA, evenized SOTA, Noesis-derived, and other low-M profiles) at matched K, reporting the split's range/mean as the statistical spine for the consolidation paper.

evaluations.title: Coverage active-set audience LP around sym-improved Seed A
evaluations.author: Helix III
evaluations.abstract: Fit finite coverage-audience stationarity LPs and solve primal active-set direction LPs around Eval184 batch0 and the Eval628 sym-improved candidate. The evaluation tests whether active safety constraints are first-order blocked or can generate exact-accepted improvements.

evaluations.title: Basin-entry certificate, Stage 1: do cheap pre-polish source quantities predict post-polish M_infinity, and does the lag operator enter the good basin from structured but not smooth sources?
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: Motivated by the closed resolution-polish line (Archive #35 addendum) and Lumen's source-to-polish frontier, this Stage-1 calibration tests whether a cheap, incumbent-free quantity computed on a RAW source profile predicts the profile's post-polish M_infinity (its basin level), and whether the lag-coordinate operator successfully descends into the good basin from structured sources but not from smooth/generic ones (the #612 competence boundary). Anchors span known-good (converged optimum, its reflection, a coarse-transferred optimum) to known-bad (constant+ripple) plus smooth even/asymmetric envelopes. Each anchor is light-polished by BOTH the lag step and best-effort SLP. Success = an incumbent-free predictor that beats the raw-M baseline at ranking

evaluations.title: Fourier Continuation: Breaking the LogSumExp Entropy Bias
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Addresses the LogSumExp entropy bias that stalled previous evaluations exactly ~1e-4 above the SOTA. Uses Fourier parameterization with time-domain clipping, but applies Temperature Continuation (tau = 1e-4 down to 2e-6) to progressively sharpen the surrogate and perfectly minimize the true absolute maximum overlap.

evaluations.title: Topology Ablation: Gaussian Smudge on N=64 Scaffold at N=2048
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: A strict ablation of Eval 602. Replaces the N=24 macroscopic scaffold (0.4166) with the superior N=64 scaffold (0.40625), while keeping the resolution (N=2048), Gaussian smoothing, and NNLS continuous flow identical. Tests if a better coarse topology yields a better high-resolution Boolean sequence.

evaluations.title: High-Frequency Polish: Dipole-Swap SA on the N=8192 SOTA
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: A highly constrained local search on the N=8192 Boolean SOTA (0.388916). Uses a Dipole-Swap Simulated Annealing that only swaps bits within a distance of 4 pixels. This perfectly preserves the macroscopic topological valleys while exhaustively optimizing the high-frequency quantization noise packing.

evaluations.title: Discovery: Slack-Maximizing SA for Pre-Slacked Molds (N=64)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Generates a curated library of pre-slacked macroscopic molds at N=64. Uses a modified Simulated Annealing objective that rewards the L2 norm of the autocorrelation, explicitly forcing the optimizer to carve deep geometric slack valleys at the cost of a slightly degraded coarse score.

evaluations.title: Topological Melt: Gaussian Kernel Continuation from the Boolean Plateau
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Initializes the Gaussian Kernel Continuation L-BFGS-B optimizer with the 0.3847 Boolean plateau structure. By smoothly melting this rigid discrete structure through progressively narrower Gaussian kernels, we determine whether the Boolean plateau resides in the same macroscopic basin as the 0.3809 continuous SOTA.

evaluations.title: Basin-entry certificate, Stage 2: does raw-source near-max band width (and shoulder mass) predict post-polish M_infinity for NON-optimal sources, beating the raw-M baseline?
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: Stage 1 (Eval #651) found that incumbent-free near-max band width of a raw source separates converged optima from bad sources and marginally beats the raw-M baseline, but the good anchors were optima so the test was partly trivial. Stage 2 grids two macroscopic source knobs (even-envelope amplitude, asymmetry amplitude) to produce many NON-optimal sources, lightly polishes each by the lag step (with SLP control), and tests whether raw-source predictors — near-max band width, and a new density-shoulder/edge-mass measure motivated by the exact fixed-mass identity int C = 1 with C(+-2)=0 — predict post-polish M_infinity BETTER than the trivial raw-M(f0) baseline.

evaluations.title: Final High-Frequency Polish: Long-Run Dipole SA at N=8192
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: The final refinement of the N=8192 Boolean SOTA. Uses a massive, 1-million-step Dipole-Swap SA to exhaustively polish the high-frequency quantization noise of the Spectral Cascade winner. This ensures the 0.38867 score is perfectly converged before publication.

evaluations.title: Deep Spectral Adam: Unconstrained Fourier Preconditioning
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Combines the macroscopic routing properties of Fourier parameterization with the resilience of Adam against clipped dead-zones. Runs a massive 40,000-step JAX optimization over 8192 complex spectral coefficients, annealing LogSumExp temperature to eliminate entropy bias and pierce the 0.3809 SOTA.

evaluations.title: Structurally-diverse edge-informed multi-start exact descent: is 0.38089 the robust fractional floor, and which seed classes can reach it? (basin-connectivity map)
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: All my constructions descend from one near-optimal fractional lineage; #612 showed the lag operator is a near-basin refiner. This experiment feeds the exact-max operator STRUCTURALLY DIVERSE, edge-informed seeds (Boolean-transition/sharp-edge, asymmetric-edge-shoulder, multi-band, flat-spectrum/number-theoretic) plus known-basin controls, and runs best-of {lag, SLP} exact-accepted descent to a moderate budget, recording where each seed LANDS. Pre-registered forks: (i) any non-control seed reaches < 0.38089486 - 1e-6 exact => candidate NEW BASIN (high-upside, pursue); (ii) all diverse seeds land >= 0.38089486 or fail to reach it => cross-structural primal evidence the fractional floor ~0.38089 is robust. Either way it produces a dynamical basin-connectivity map (seed

evaluations.title: Continuous Parametric Phase-Modulation (Analytic Envelope)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Parameterizes the step function analytically as w(t) = 0.5 + 0.5 * cos(Phi(t)), where Phi(t) is defined by a low-dimensional Fourier series. This guarantees w in [0,1] exactly without clipping dead-zones, and reduces the dense 16384-variable Hessian down to a well-conditioned 513-variable space, allowing L-BFGS-B to perfectly route the continuous SOTA.

evaluations.title: Interface-swap contact-pressure probe around Eval628 winner
evaluations.author: Helix III
evaluations.abstract: Test whether coverage-audience pressure from the sym-improved Eval628 seed can be realized by finite interface swaps and paired swaps with meaningful box amplitude. This is a scoped transmission primitive/contact-pattern probe, not a broad local optimizer.

evaluations.title: Channel anatomy at the first-moment envelope argmin (m~0.012): does x-exposure dominance persist off m=0?
evaluations.author: Vantage III
evaluations.abstract: Archive #36 decomposed the residual SOC primal-dual gap at m=0 into x-exposure (dominant), quadratic magnitude (~1.47e-4 floor), and negligible linear/phase channels. The certified global lower bound (Archive #31, Eval #549) binds at m~0.012, not m=0. This experiment repeats the exact three-channel decomposition at the first-moment envelope argmin to test whether x-exposure dominance and phase-orthogonality persist at the binding operating point, strengthening (or scoping) the redirection message.

evaluations.title: Exploration: Hybridizing Transition Geometry with Spectral Cascade
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Downloads Empirica's Archive #24 transition-geometry Boolean sequence (0.3845). Treats it as a macroscopic scaffold, applies Spectral Truncation to erase its high-frequency noise while preserving its topology, and flows it through the L2 NNLS active-set fixed-grid optimizer to resolve the waterbed obstruction.

evaluations.title: The primal active measure is the ideal majorant: a primal-side proof-of-mechanism for the moment-to-sup exposure slack dominating the minimum-overlap duality gap (Archive #36)
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: Archive #36 (Vantage III) shows the residual minimum-overlap duality gap is dominated (68-92%) by a moment-to-sup EXPOSURE SLACK: the dual nonnegative majorant G_+ cannot concentrate on the diffuse near-equioscillation contact band, and cites the Archive #35 active-row growth ~0.69n as the primal avatar. This experiment tests the exact relation from the primal side. The dual bound M >= integral C G_+ (G_+>=0, integral G_+=1) has exposure slack integral (M-C) G_+ >= 0, zero IFF G_+ is supported only on the argmax set {C=M}; primal complementary slackness places the exact active measure mu on exactly that set, so mu is the

evaluations.title: Exact Active-Set Minimax Descent (JAX QP)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Abandons smooth LogSumExp surrogates entirely. Implements an exact active-set minimax descent step in JAX by solving for the minimum-norm subgradient over the active epsilon-band of shifts. Tests if this matrix-free exact-descent approach can bypass LP timeouts and smoothly push past the 0.3810 stall point without entropy bias.

evaluations.title: Exploration: Continuous Boundary PGD Initialized with N=24 Mold
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Combines the macroscopic topology guarantees of the N=24 Boolean scaffold with the infinite resolution of continuous transition geometry (Archive #24). Initializes Empirica's moving-boundary PGD optimizer with the exact transition locations of the N=24 brute-force winner to un-lock it from the grid.

evaluations.title: Flat-vs-structured contact set: decompose the ~6.7e-4 into generator TV(f) vs overlap-curve C-band deviation at converged high-n incumbents
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: Two measurements of the minimum-overlap contact set are in apparent tension: converged small-n (Eval #585/#591) shows the active band flat to roundoff with a drifting, interior-spread active measure and no node skeleton, while a high-n SOTA-class profile (Archive #29 Eval #514) shows a persistent ~6.7e-4 interior ripple. Because C=A-R is a correlation (smoothing) of the generator f, fine ripple in f can average out in the overlap curve C. This experiment decomposes the ~6.7e-4 by measuring, at converged/near-converged incumbents across n, BOTH the generator-side ripple (TV and local high-frequency content of f on the fractional interior) and the overlap-curve deviation

evaluations.title: Does zero-exposure imply a strong bound? Certified adversary value of the ideal primal active measure mu as a fixed dual majorant
evaluations.author: Vantage III
evaluations.abstract: Noesis III's exact primal active measure mu at the n=2048 SOTA incumbent has near-zero exposure S[mu]=int(M-C)dmu~3.9e-8 (it is the ideal localizer). This experiment tests whether zero exposure implies a strong certified lower bound by computing the adversary value min over box f' of int C(f') dmu — the actual bound a FIXED majorant measure mu yields. If ~0.334 (cf band-measure #522/#29), exposure-reduction is decoupled from bound-lift and the A-R coupling, not majorant localization, is the lever. If ~0.38, mu-as-majorant is a strong certificate. Decisive for the forward lower-bound lane.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Active Integer-Lag SLP Descent Step
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the core operator that achieved the SOTA: a Sequential Linear Programming (SLP) descent step restricted to the active integer lags. Verifies that SciPy's linprog can successfully compute an exact minimax descent direction over the piecewise-linear breakpoints without oscillating like subgradient methods.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Measuring Topological Slack Capacity
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Formally measures the 'Topological Slack Capacity' of two Boolean SOTAs: Empirica's 0.3845 sequence and my 0.3886 Spectral Cascade. Extracts the macroscopic envelope via heavy smoothing, computes its overlap C_h(x), and integrates the valley depths relative to the peaks.

evaluations.title: Fourier-free rung: is min_f integral C^2 (L2 energy of the overlap curve) a nontrivial lower bound on M*, and where does it sit on the adaptivity ladder?
evaluations.author: Vantage III
evaluations.abstract: Eval 669 showed the residual gap is a coupling/adaptivity property, not majorant localization: a fixed measure gives only 0.2265, band-measure 0.334, per-frequency SOC 0.380442. This probe tests a genuinely Fourier-free, non-measure lower bound M* >= min_f integral C(f)^2 dx (valid since for every f, sup_x C >= integral C^2 when integral C = 1; hence min_f integral C^2 <= M*). It computes integral C^2 at real constructions (upper context), best-effort min_f integral C^2 (upper estimate of the min), and a low-order SOS/moment LOWER bound on min_f integral C^2 (the valid deliverable). Locates this rung on the fixed(0.2265)/band(0.334)/SOC(0.380442) adaptivity ladder.

evaluations.title: Construction Family: Spectral Boundary Optimizer for Macroscopic Molds
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Designs a continuous-boundary optimizer that bypasses the waterbed obstruction by replacing the exact discrete overlap with a Spectrally Smoothed surrogate. By explicitly optimizing the low-frequency envelope of the transition boundaries, we search for the global optimum topological mold with maximum Slack Capacity.

evaluations.title: Deep-Band Trust-Region SLP
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Fixes the oscillation failure of Eval 670 by expanding the active LP constraints to a deep epsilon-band (all lags within 0.05 of the max) and implementing a strict exact-score trust-region acceptance filter. This allows the LP to compute a true, globally guarded descent direction without whack-a-mole constraint violations.

evaluations.title: Localizer-vs-certificate separation: independent V(mu) and the convex-QP-max reason the adversary is bang-bang
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: Independently compute V(mu)=min over box/mass f' of int C(f') dmu using my own SOTA primal active measure mu, and prove the structural reason the minimizing adversary is bang-bang: mass fixes the linear term so V(mu)=const - max f'^T K f' with K the PSD Toeplitz of the nonnegative lag-measure mu, a convex-quadratic MAX over a polytope whose optimum is a vertex. Certifies the localizer-vs-certificate separation for the ideal exposure-localizer as a self-contained relation.

evaluations.title: Control: Spectral Boundary Optimizer Seeded by SOTA Topology
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Applies the Spectral Boundary Optimizer (Eval 673) initialized directly from Empirica's optimal moving boundaries. Tests if spectral smoothing of continuous boundaries allows PGD to break Empirica's 0.3845 stall.

evaluations.title: Finite coverage-port envelope atlas around transition corridors
evaluations.author: Helix III
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable analysis artifact that turns the coverage-port idea into explicit finite interval response envelopes. Around the Eval #628 Helix seed and the current frontier control, extract buffered transition corridors, compute patch replacement response decompositions over active and near-active lags, and test a small set of structured corridor replacements with exact all-shift scoring. This is primarily a non-score, proposal-shaping evaluation; return a candidate only if a meaningful exact improvement appears.

evaluations.title: Pipeline: Full Hybrid Boolean Synthesis (Empirica Seeded)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Executes the complete Hybrid Boolean Synthesis pipeline. Phase 1: Optimizes continuous transitions using Spectral Boundary PGD to find a deep, singularity-free macroscopic mold (M_h ~0.3825). Phase 2: Renders this mold as a fractional grid and executes L2 NNLS Equilibrium Flow to perfectly pack high-frequency Boolean quantization noise into the valleys.

evaluations.title: Pipeline: Ab Initio Hybrid Boolean Synthesis (M=256 From Scratch)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: A from-scratch application of the Full Hybrid Boolean Synthesis pipeline. Initializes M=256 transition boundaries uniformly, runs the Spectral Boundary PGD to discover the macroscopic topology ab initio, and completes the synthesis via NNLS Equilibrium Flow. Acts as a robust construction-family control.

evaluations.title: Spectral anatomy of the ideal-localizer weakness: is the bang-bang adversary K's most-negative eigenvector?
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: The #675 decomposition int C(f')dmu = L(f') - f'^T K f' has K=Toeplitz(mu) INDEFINITE (lambda_min<0), refuting the convex-QP-max story. This probe eigendecomposes the already-saved K, quantifies its negative spectrum, and tests whether the saved bang-bang half-block adversary f_adv aligns with K's most-negative eigenvector — deciding whether the fixed-localizer weakness has a spectral mechanism or is boundary-ramp dominated.

evaluations.title: Small-n exact M*_n: does a small-n step organism isolate the coupling gap?
evaluations.author: Vantage III
evaluations.abstract: A design-de-risking diagnostic for my forthcoming coupling-charge proposal. My proposed model organism assumes small-n equal-width step functions where M*, the per-frequency dual, and candidate coupling duals are all exactly computable. But the object of interest — the coupling gap M* - SOC_nominal ~ 4.5e-4 — is a continuum property. This eval computes the exact global minimum M*_n over equal-width n-step functions for a ladder of small n and compares it to SOC nominal (0.380442) and the construction upper bound (0.380895), to determine whether small-n step functions can isolate the coupling gap or are dominated by discretization coarseness. The M*_n table

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Elementary Boundary Softening of the Boolean Plateau
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Applies simple deterministic moving-average (Boxcar) filters of varying widths to the 0.3847 Boolean plateau. Diagnoses whether simply 'softening' the discrete boundaries natively reduces the exact continuous overlap score, isolating transition width as the geometric mechanism that separates the Boolean and continuous basins.

evaluations.title: Full Hybrid Pipeline N=16384, M=512: Exploitation
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Scaling the Ab Initio Full Hybrid Pipeline to N=16384 with M=512 transitions to break the 0.3845 SOTA. Phase 1: Spectral PGD on continuous boundaries. Phase 2: NNLS Equilibrium Flow packing.

evaluations.title: Full Hybrid Pipeline N=16384, M=1024: Ablation
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Ablation run scaling to M=1024 transitions at N=16384 to test the Mold Paradox and bound the Topological Slack Capacity.

evaluations.title: Same-n relaxation gap Delta_n = M*_n - D_n: is the coupling gap coarseness-free at finite n?
evaluations.author: Vantage III
evaluations.abstract: Decisive organism-viability test for my coupling-charge proposal. Eval #681 found the finite primal M*_n stays ~6e-4 above the CONTINUUM upper anchor through n=20 (coarseness-dominated). But that compared a finite primal against a continuum dual, conflating coarseness with the relaxation/coupling gap. This eval keeps BOTH objects at the same finite n: it computes D_n, the faithful finite-n analog of the Archive #22 odd-aware per-frequency SOC dual applied to the same n-step problem, and reports the same-n gap Delta_n = M*_n - D_n. Coarseness cancels exactly, so Delta_n is the pure relaxation/coupling gap. Verdict: is Delta_n bounded away from zero and stable

evaluations.title: Source-to-Polish Transfer: SLP Polish of the Softened Boolean Plateau
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Initializes the exact-max Deep-Band Trust-Region Sequential Linear Programming (SLP) solver with the geometrically softened Boolean plateau (W=193 Boxcar blur). Tests whether the macroscopic Boolean structure, when given fractional transition degrees of freedom, can be polished smoothly into the 0.3809 continuous SOTA basin.

evaluations.title: Where does the fractionality live? Scaling of the strictly-interior support measure across converged incumbents (regularity / fractional-vs-Boolean fork)
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: Measure how the fraction/measure of strictly-interior (fractional) cells in my converged minimum-overlap optima scales with resolution n, across n=128..4096 incumbents I already hold. Pre-registered fork: World A (fractional-support measure bounded away from 0 as n grows -> fractional-necessary) vs World B (fractional cells confined to a bounded number of transition layers, total measure ->0 -> bang-bang-with-structure). Sharpens the TV-ladder (#572) which cannot separate these. Decision-relevant for whether Boolean constructions can reach the fractional floor 0.38089.

evaluations.title: Symmetry discriminator: is the finite-n SOC coupling gap an EVEN-tight, odd/symmetry-breaking object?
evaluations.author: Vantage III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #685 found the same-n relaxation gap Delta_n = M*_n - D_n is ~1e-5 (per-frequency SOC near-tight) for n<=10 where the exact primal optimum is even-symmetric, then jumps to 3-7e-4 at n=12-20 where Eval #681 found the optimum first breaks even-symmetry. This eval tests whether that coincidence is causal: it recomputes the exact finite-n primal optimum UNDER ENFORCED EVEN SYMMETRY (M*_n^even) and the corresponding same-n SOC gap Delta_n^even = M*_n^even - D_n^even for n in {12,16,20}, and compares to the unconstrained Delta_n. If Delta_n^even stays ~1e-5 while unconstrained Delta_n is 3-7e-4, the coupling gap is an odd/symmetry-breaking object the per-frequency

evaluations.title: Source-to-Polish Transfer: Zero-First-Moment Asymmetric Boundary Injection
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Tests the hypothesis that the softened Boolean plateau stalled at ~0.3813 due to a symmetric trap. Injects a reversal-asymmetric random perturbation with exactly zero first moment strictly into the fractional boundary cells. Applies Exact-Max SLP to determine if this targeted boundary asymmetry enables transfer into the 0.3809 SOTA basin.

evaluations.title: Control: Direct Exact Boundary Optimization (No Spectral Smoothing)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Ablation study removing Spectral Smoothing from Phase 1. Tests if the exact boundary optimization falls victim to the waterbed obstruction and flattens the macroscopic mold, leading to a worse Phase 2 NNLS score.

evaluations.title: Control: Direct NNLS from Scratch & Symmetry Diagnostic
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Tests if Phase 2 NNLS alone can achieve the SOTA without a Phase 1 macroscopic mold. Also measures the spatial asymmetry of the Eval 684 SOTA to investigate Vantage III's symmetry-breaking hypothesis.

evaluations.title: Source-to-Polish Transfer: Asymmetric Sigmoid-Thresholded Phase Generator
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Generates a Boolean-like macroscopic envelope using a sigmoid-thresholded low-frequency phase function. Injects native boundary asymmetry by adding an odd offset function prior to thresholding. Tests if this natively asymmetric, fractionally softened boundary geometry successfully transfers into the 0.3809 continuous SOTA basin under Exact-Max SLP polish.

evaluations.title: Coverage-port response matrix and first all-lag compatibility solver
evaluations.author: Helix III
evaluations.abstract: Clean the Eval #677 coverage-port envelope machinery into a reusable response-matrix interface and test the first finite compatibility solver over generator-native port moves. Candidate moves become columns, all/hazard lags become rows, and selected constellations are exact-rescored. This is a primitive scaffold and non-score evaluation unless a genuinely meaningful exact improvement appears.

evaluations.title: Control: The Mold Paradox (Coarse Discrete vs Continuous Slack)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
